articleTitle: Enhancing Performance of Doubly-Fed Induction Generator Under Unbalanced Condition Using Multi-Stage Control
abstract: The doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) is very sensitive to unbalanced voltage as it induces large and unbalanced emf in the stator and rotor windings. As a result, double grid frequency oscillation (DGFO) appears in stator and rotor current, electromagnetic torque, active and reactive power, and DC-link voltage. These adverse effects reduce the life span and performance of the DFIG under unbalanced network conditions. In order to minimize oscillation and improve the performance of DFIG under unbalanced network conditions, this paper proposes a multi-stage control based on the level of voltage unbalance at the point of common coupling (PCC). The proposed control includes the three stages. Control stage 1 is responsible for minimizing oscillation in the operating quantities of DFIG by reducing the negative sequence rotor current with the help of the rotor side converter (RSC). Control stage 2 further reduces the oscillation by minimizing the voltage unbalance at the PCC with the help of a grid-side converter (GSC). Control stage 3 minimizes the oscillation in DC-link voltage with the help of a battery connected across the DC link. The proposed algorithm is validated on the Real-time Digital Simulator (RTDS).

articleTitle: Adaptive Disturbance Onset Detection in Power System with Varying Wind Power Penetration Using Kernel Density Estimator
abstract: The accurate detection of disturbance onset is crucial when employing polynomial curve fitting for rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) and inertia estimation. This detection aids in selecting the appropriate window length for approximating the system's inertial response. Existing literature either assumes that onset instant is known or uses fixed RoCoF thresholding to detect the disturbance onset. Since modern power systems consist of renewable-based power generation which has variable inertia, a fixed RoCoF thresholding approach is no longer suitable for detecting the onset. In this view, the paper proposes a kernel density estimator (KDE) based adaptive onset detection approach that performs consistently for systems with varying levels of wind power penetration irrespective of the magnitude of disturbance and area under disturbance. The effectiveness of the proposed KDE is validated for three different test scenarios of a modified IEEE 4-machine, 11-bus system viz. with only synchronous generation, 10% and 20% wind energy integration.

articleTitle: DTC Implementation on SRM Using Mid-Point Converter: Simulation and Experimental Validation
abstract: Switched Reluctance Motors (SRMs) are known for their durable design, rendering them well-suited for demanding environments and high-speed operations. They offer advantages such as high torque density and fault tolerance, making them increasingly favored in electric vehicle propulsion systems and industrial automation. However, their inherent drawback of high torque ripple limits their applicability. This research endeavors to address this limitation by proposing a novel approach exploring the integration of Direct Torque Control (DTC) with a Mid-Point converter designed for 8/6 SRMs, aiming to enhance motor performance and reduction in torque ripple. The implementation of a mid-point converter, which employs fewer switches, helps reduce losses, while DTC is utilized to minimize torque ripple and acoustic noise. The DTC control strategy is initially simulated using MATLAB Simulink and subsequently experimentally validated with the TI28379D DSP controller.

articleTitle: Load Frequency and Tieline Power Management of Renewable Energy Based Two Area Microgrid with Virtual Inertia Control
abstract: Effective load frequency management is a crucial element of microgrid, especially when including renewable energy sources (RESs). This article discusses the regulation of frequency in a microgrid with multi areas and multiple RESs. It proposes a new control technique called the hippopotamus optimization algorithm (HOA)-based cascaded fractional order proportional-integral (FOPI)-PI derivative with filter (C-FOPI-PIDN) controller. Comparing the HOA approach with other algorithms, it is shown that the C-FOPI-PIDN controller works better than the FOPID and PIDN controllers in terms of overshoot, undershoot, and settling time for frequency and tie-line power variances. The suggested system consists of a two-area microgrid that incorporates biodiesel, biogas, diesel generators, and photovoltaic systems. In order to efficiently handle the fluctuations caused by the integration of RESs, the implementation of virtual inertia control (VIC) with an energy storage system effectively manages oscillations. The results are verified by the utilization of both MATLAB Simulink and the OPAL-RT (OP4510) platform.

articleTitle: Oscillation Damping in Grid-Scale Virtual Energy Storage System with Renewable Energy Penetration
abstract: Reduction in inertia of power system becomes crucial factor due to increasing integration of power electronics based renewable energy sources. So synthesis of inertia or providing virtual inertia by using energy storage system (ESS) is adopted to enhance inertial power reserve capacity of the grid. This regulates frequency after load disturbances. However using ESS to provide inertia has its own challenges such as space and cost constraints, charging and discharging delay of batteries etc. Thus providing inertial power without energy storage devices, called as virtual energy storage, is an alternative. But this introduces phase lag to the system due to use of dead zone in feed back path and increases oscillations in frequency, tie line power flow and area control error. To address this, a lead compensator is proposed in this article. Calculation of exact parameters of the compensator is shown in details. This compensator reduces oscillations without affecting the system's virtual energy storage capability, which will be discussed in detail in the following section. The performance of the proposed compensator is verified in MATLAB/SIMULINK platform. The result shows complete damp out of oscillations after contigency.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Subsequent Commutation Failure in Dual Infeed LCC HVDC Connected to the Weak Grid by Adopting Hybrid Infeed HVDC
abstract: This paper aims to propose LCC-VSC hybrid infeed HVDC systems to mitigate the risk of subsequent commutation failure in dual-infeed LCC HVDC connected to a weak AC grid. When the inverter side AC grid is subjected to a temporary fault, the LCC converter demands a high amount of reactive power and stable AC voltage with less harmonic distortion during recovery for successful commutation. The paper discusses how adopting AC voltage control mode aided with harmonic compensation control can help enhance the power stability, effective short circuit ratio and mitigate the risk of subsequent commutation failure. The proposed system is simulated and validated in MATLAB/SIMULNIK.

articleTitle: Direct Torque Control of 8/6 Switched Reluctance Motor for Improved Torque Per Ampere
abstract: In this paper, direct torque control (DTC) of four phase switched reluctance motor (SRM) for improved torque per ampere is discussed. In conventional DTC, torque and flux linkage magnitude is controlled which results in production of negative torque which reduces torque per ampere. This paper introduces a DTC where flux hysteresis loop is removed. Moreover, new voltage vectors are developed to ensure that negative torque is not produced and torque per ampere is improved. Modeling of SRM is done in MATLAB/Simulink and the proposed control algorithm is also verified. Simulation results shows that torque per ampere in the case of proposed DTC is improved compared to conventional DTC. The proposed DTC is also implemented on DSP based experimental setup.

articleTitle: Passivity Based Controller for the Three-Level Boost Converter: The Hamiltonian Framework
abstract: This paper explores the idea of passivity-based controller in the Hamiltonian framework for the three-level (TL) boost PFC converter as it is used to reduce filter size and voltage stress of switches. To implement the passivity-based controller, a Hamiltonian model of the TL boost converter is developed. Further, the performances of the controller are examined through MATLAB software and validated through real time simulator (OP-5142) as well. Based on the simulation studies the comparative discussions are carried out against the benchmark PI controller.

articleTitle: Grid Resilience Through Digital Twin and PMU Integration: A System Identification Approach
abstract: Digital Twin (DT) technology represents a significant advancement in development of self-healing power grids. DTs represent virtual replicas of physical system, thereby enabling real-time simulation, prediction, and optimization of grid performance. This paper realises a digital twin of power system by implementing state of the art System Identification Techniques (SIT) for various components in the system. The SIT is driven by data from Phasor Measurement Units (PMU). The dynamic model of generator, R-X-B parameters of transmission line, and parameters of static load model are estimated. The proposed method is a precursor to conduct steady state and dynamic analysis to respond to contingency and other low probability events, hence improving grid resiliency. The integration of DT technology with PMU measurements not only improves the self-healing capabilities of power grids but also contributes to more resilient and efficient energy systems.

articleTitle: Implementation and Performance Evaluation of Diode Failure Detection Algorithm of Diode Failure Detection Relay for Brushless Excitation System
abstract: Brushless Excitation Systems have been widely used in Synchronous Generators as it reduces the losses, maintenance and improves the reliability of the system by eliminating the usage of commutator, brushes and slip rings. Rotating diode bridge rectifier is the main part of brushless excitation system. Due to aging phenomenon and continuous process regime, the diode in the rotating bridge rectifier can fail either due to open circuit or short circuit. If such a failure prolonged, the Automatic Voltage Regulator (AVR) as well as the Exciter winding can be damaged. This paper briefly describes the structure of Brushless Excitation System technology and its operation. The paper presents the modeling of Brushless Excitation System in Real Time Digital Simulator (RTDS) and simulations carried out to study the behavior of system during the diode open circuit condition and short circuit condition in a rotating bridge rectifier. It describes the technique/principle established for detecting a diode failure condition and its validation using RTDS. It also describes the suitable hardware architecture consisting of Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) & Processor module chosen to implement the developed diode failure detection algorithm. The paper summarizes the implementation of developed algorithm on hardware and the performance evaluation carried out through Hardware-In-Loop (HIL) testing using RTDS. It also presents the various tests carried out to evaluate the performance of developed detection relay on test bed of Brushless Excitation System.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Modified TDF-IMC for a DC-DC Buck Converter
abstract: This work presents a simulation-based study for the output voltage regulation of a non-ideal DC-DC buck converter. A modified two-degree-of-freedom internal model controller (MTDF-IMC) is designed for set-point tracking and disturbance rejection. The motivation for selecting an MTDF-IMC approach lies in the fact that it can easily handle the set-point tracking and the load-disturbance rejection separately. The presented controller is tested with (i) sudden input voltage variation, (ii) parametric uncertainty in the plant model, and (iii) presence of step disturbances to showcase the effectiveness and supremacy of the proposed work. The performance of the designed controller is compared with the TDF-IMC and IMC-PID control strategies, and the results show that the designed MTDF-IMC controller outperforms TDF-IMC and IMC-PID control strategies.

Author Keywords: two-degree of freedom internal model control

articleTitle: Optimization of Droop Controlled Islanded Microgrid System with Load Models Considering Power Loss and Node Voltage Deviation
abstract: In an islanded microgrid (IMG) system, the dispatchable distributed generation (DDG) units operate in droop mode to maintain the power balance. Hence, a deviation in the voltage and frequency from nominal values takes place to satisfy the system's needs. The load behavior along with the droop characteristics of DDG units are related to the voltage and frequency of the system. This paper presents the optimum droop parameters of DDG units in the IMG system for various load models. The active and reactive power droop values and voltage reference settings of DDG units for various load models are determined by considering power loss and node voltage deviation objectives. The objectives are normalized using a fuzzy approach, and the combined objective is solved by the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. The objectives and droop parameters are displayed for constant power (CP) and voltage dependent load models. The minimum power loss and higher droop parameters are observed in a system with a constant impedance (CZ) load model. Also, the variation in active power load and active power loss with different system voltages for each load model is noticed in the 33-bus IMG system.

articleTitle: Optimal Parameter Extraction and Performance Evaluation of Empirical Polarization Curve Model for Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cell
abstract: In this study, a simplified empirical polarization curve model for PEMFCs is developed. Experimental data is collected using the Nexa 1200 PEMFC test system. The model parameters are obtained through a nonlinear optimization process conducted in MATLAB. The model is validated in the long run, showing a low Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), a high R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> value, and a close match between the experimental stack voltage and the modeled stack voltage. Moreover, the variation of polarization losses (activation, ohmic, and concentration) with stack current is analyzed. In addition, the model performance is studied on reduced datasets showcasing satisfactory performance for moderate reduction, thus demonstrating the robustness and predictive performance of PEMFC under different operating conditions.

articleTitle: Improving Wind Turbine Fault Ride-Through with Combined STATCOM and Battery Storage
abstract: STATCOM (Static Synchronous Compensator) and Battery Storage Systems (BSS) are commonly employed to improve performance under faulty conditions and enhance wind farm stability. This paper investigates the integration of a BSS, operating in an advanced Grid-Following (GFL) mode, with a STATCOM connected to a Doubly-Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) wind turbine. The study focuses on transient improvements by integrating STATCOM with BSS, aiding voltage and frequency stability within the wind farm network. It examines the impact of STATCOM and BSS in integrated and independent modes on voltage and frequency at the Point of Common Coupling (PCC) bus. The study highlights the ride-through capability of wind turbines with STATCOM and BSS during faults and load variations. Extensive DFIG-based wind turbine system simulations analyze voltage dips under three configurations: standalone STATCOM, standalone BSS, and combined STATCOM and BSS. The simulations and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing, conducted using a Real-Time Digital Simulator (RTDS), demonstrate that the integrated STATCOM and BSS offer superior transient stability and fault ride-through capabilities, maintaining voltage and frequency stability better than independent systems.

articleTitle: Decentralized Energy Trading with Smart Contracts in Blockchain Ecosystem
abstract: There has been substantial and incremental penetration of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) in the energy market. Growing number of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) is paving way for more generation entities latching on to the distribution systems. Today, relevance of prosumer is fast gaining popularity as compared to conventional producers, due to inherent ability to produce as well as to consume power. Therefore, decentralized power generation with prosumers within neighbourhood is gaining traction. Especially, contribution of wind and solar generations in overall power mix has been evolving. Energy trading using conventional Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) between producers and consumers are currently notarised manual agreements, which is vulnerable to tampering, thefts, inflicted destructions, foisted litigations, faces non compliance issues, non accessibility to all stakeholders etc. In order to obviate conventional forms of executing manual PPAs, it is imperative to resort to proliferated technologies of Internet of Things (IoTs) and use of blockchain applications. Use of smart contracts, particularly in energy trading sector is still niche. Energy trading with blockchain enables speedy, secure, concurrent, decentralised, transparent, fair transactive Peer-to-Peer (P2P) trading. In this paper, P2P trading among prosumer, consumer and microgrid operator has been evolved using MATLAB, Python Web 3.0 and Remix Ethereum IDE. The smart contract using blockchain in times ahead will be disruptive, thus replacing legacy systems of contract management.

articleTitle: Detection of False Command Injection Attack on Phase Shifting Transformer Using Supervised Learning
abstract: The paper presents False Command Injection Attacks (FCIAs) on Phase Shifting Transformers (PSTs) tap. FCIAs targeting PSTs can lead to the overloading of transmission lines and potentially trigger circuit breaker disconnections. The incorporation of measurement and communication devices increases the susceptibility of power systems to cyber-attacks. Adversaries can stealthily manipulate measurements from Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs), bypassing Bad Data Detectors (BDDs). To identify FCIAs on PST taps, supervised learning is used. The authors show that the models are accurate in detecting FCIAs by training them on labeled datasets that include both authentic and attacked tap settings. Features extraction is performed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) on the extensive measurements. The FCIA generation and detection are implemented in Matpower and Python and are tested on the standard IEEE 118 bus system.

articleTitle: Graph Theoretic Approach Based Cyber Contingency Assessment of Smart Power Grids
abstract: The rapid advancement of information and communication technologies and their widespread integration into power systems has transformed modern grids into Cyber- Physical Power Systems (CPPS) also known as smart grids. Owing to the strong interdependence, cyber anomalies can have a significant impact on the physical power grid. Hence, it is essential to evaluate and prioritize cyber contingencies. This paper introduces a novel approach for quantifying cyber contingencies, employing the Cyber Contingency Quantifying Measure (CCQM) derived through the Cyber-Restrained Optimal Power Flow (CROPF) problem. The graph theoretic approach is used to model the cyber-physical smart grid. This approach does not require complex and computationally intensive cyber-physical co-simulations. The proposed algorithm's effectiveness has been assessed through practical demonstrations on two standard test systems. These results illustrate the proposed approach's efficacy in efficiently prioritizing cyber contingencies and accurately quantifying their impact on the energy grid.

articleTitle: Condition Monitoring of Overhead Line Insulators Using a Hybrid Deep Learning Approach
abstract: Insulators play a pivotal role in ensuring the safe and efficient operation of transmission lines, preventing high-voltage electricity from leaking to the ground, or other structures. Thus, their protection and monitoring are of prime importance. In this paper, a hybrid-YOLOv8n (You Only Look Once) model has been proposed for detection and classification of faulty insulators in aerial images, utilizing a ResNet-50 v1.5 as a feature extractor. Metrics such as precision, recall, and mAP (Mean Average Precision) have been used for evaluation. The model has been compared with other models, including a stand-alone YOLOv8m and a hybrid YOLOv8m with a ResNet-50 v1.5 feature extractor.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling of Wind Speed for Loss Reduction in Mesh Distribution Systems Using Long Short-Term Memory Network
abstract: Electric power systems are experiencing rapid growth in size and complexity due to rising global demand, placing significant stress on power distribution networks. This presents challenges such as minimizing line losses, optimizing voltage profiles, and reducing operational costs. To address these issues, Distributed Generation (DG) technologies, particularly wind energy, are being integrated into distribution systems. However, the unpredictable nature of wind introduces variability in power generation, making accurate forecasting essential. This study employs a Long-Short Term Memory (LSTM) model for multivariate wind speed forecasting, specifically targeting Telangana, India [18.112° N, 79.0193° E]. The model's accuracy is evaluated using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). The forecasted wind speed data is then used to estimate power output, which is incorporated into the distribution system. Additionally, load flow analysis, utilizing the current injection method, is performed on an IEEE-136 bus-balanced Mesh Distribution System (MDS) to evaluate power losses in wind-powered DG setups. This work provides valuable insights for optimizing the integration of renewable energy into power grids.

articleTitle: Development and Experimental Validation of Cubic-Spline Based Flexible Power Point Tracking for Photovoltaic Systems Under Partial Shading
abstract: Conventional maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithms are limited in their ability to support the grid. In contrast, flexible power point tracking (FPPT) algorithms can effectively regulate the output of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, enabling essential grid support functions such as enhancing grid frequency and virtual inertia. Although partial shading is a common issue in solar PV systems, conventional FPPT algorithms are not fully efficient in providing all FPPT functionalities including power reserve control (PRC), power limiting control (PLC), power ramp rate control (PRRC), and MPPT control under non-uniform variation of solar irradiation. This paper proposes a cubic-spline-based improved FPPT algorithm for both uniform and nonuniform variations of solar irradiation. The performance of the proposed cubic-spline-based improved FPPT algorithm has been validated using simulations performed in MATLAB/SIMULINK and experimental hardware. Further-more, in order to have a fair comparison, the performance of the proposed cubic-spline-based improved FPPT algorithm has been compared with that of the conventional FPPT algorithm. Simulations and experimental validation results revealed the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed FPPT algorithm in providing faster response time and low power oscillation during steady state and transient variation of solar irradiation.

articleTitle: Real-Time Man in the Middle Attack Detection and Mitigation in Cyber-Physical Systems Using Neural Networks and Remote Monitoring
abstract: This article presents a novel method for detecting and mitigating Man-in-the-Middle (MIM) attacks in cyber-physical systems (CPS) using neural networks. MIM attacks are particularly dangerous because attackers can intercept and manipulate communications, gaining control over secure data. Existing detection tools often require high computational resources and are costly. Our approach focuses on a DC-DC converter, a crucial CPS component, where the wireless communication controller is an Arduino Nano IoT, and real-time monitoring is enabled via a LabVIEW GUI on a remote PC. We developed a neural network-based detection system to identify abnormal behavior indicative of MIM attacks. The results demonstrate its effectiveness in maintaining system integrity and reliability. Additionally, we explore a remote monitoring method as an alternative to the LabVIEW GUI, enhancing flexibility and scalability. The control algorithm is developed in MATLAB 2022a, with real-time hardware implementation validating the proposed method.

articleTitle: Enhancing Frequency Stability in Microgrids with MPC-Based Virtual Inertia Controller
abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources (RESs) into power systems has significantly increased to meet growing energy demands and address environmental concerns. This trend has led to the more prevalent islanded operation of power grids as microgrids <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{Gs})$</tex>. While beneficial, this shift results in a reduced inertia constant due to high levels of RES penetration and islanded operations, causing deteriorated frequency stability and higher rates of change of frequency (RoCoF). This paper investigates the effectiveness of a model predictive control (MPC) based virtual inertia (VI) system to enhance frequency stability in isolated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \text{Gs}$</tex> with high RES penetration. A comprehensive MATLAB/Simulink model was developed to compare the MPC-based VI controller against conventional VI control, as well as PI and PID-based VI control methods, under various operating conditions and load/RES power variations. Optimal parameters for the MPC-based VI control system were determined using Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) techniques, while PI and PID gains were tuned using the MATLAB-based internal model control (IMC) method. Simulation results validate that the MPC-based VI controller offers more reliable and precise frequency regulation, significantly enhancing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{G}$</tex> stability and resilience under diverse disturbances and operating conditions. For instance, under normal conditions with a solar power deviation of 0.02 p.u., the frequency deviation with the MPC controller was 0.0045 Hz, compared to 0.0259 Hz, 0.0178 Hz, and 0.0047 Hz for the conventional, PI, and PID controllers, respectively. Histogram analysis further supports these findings, showing lower standard deviations and average frequency deviations for the MPC controller across all operating conditions. Overall, the MPC-based VI controller effectively improves frequency stability and resilience in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{G}$</tex> with high-RES penetrations.

articleTitle: Intra-State Security Constrained Economic Despatch (SCED) in India - A way Forward
abstract: India has a complex federal structure for electricity governance, where both the Central and State Governments have jurisdiction over electricity, making it a Concurrent Subject. India has adopted a decentralized, multilateral, and coordinated scheduling model. States follow a merit order-based scheduling (MoD) system, which prioritizes the least cost approach to meet demand from contracted capacities. Security Constrained Economic Despatch (SCED) at the national level has demonstrated significant efficiencies and economic benefits. It is now the time to start implementation of Intra-State SCED in States that have internal generations that could be optimized for economic benefits. The basic implementation requirements are studied and detailed in this paper with the aim to facilitate the implementation of Intra-State SCED. A simulation study has been carried out taking input from the data available in the MERIT India App to find out the possible savings through the implementation of Intra-State SCED and subsequent integration at the Regional and National level. A brief set of results is presented which shows substantial savings after the integration of States at the Regional and National Level. Overall, this translates to total cost savings of approximately ₹95 to ₹160 lakh per hour during off-peak and peak hours, respectively.

articleTitle: Planning Distribution System Upgrades with EV Adoption: An Indian Military Station Case Study
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) adoption may lead to increased thermal violations in the transformers and lines as well as increased voltage violations in distribution systems, necessitating asset upgrades. This paper presents a methodology for planning the distribution system upgrade due to EV adoption in a phased manner on an electrical distribution network. Specifically, this work identifies the 3 types of distribution network assets that may be constrained and need upgrade, i.e., distribution transformers, distribution lines, and capacitor banks, by performing an impact assessment at the asset level. The uncertainty in EV adoption and user behaviors is incorporated through Monte Carlo simulations, and thereby, two upgradation strategies are developed for a planner, i.e., aggressive and conservative. Further, two coordinated charging schemes are suggested to mitigate or defer the costly asset upgrade to later years. The cost-benefit analysis is presented to demonstrate if the coordinated charging schemes can reduce the financial burden of asset upgrades compared to the business-as-usual EV charging. The proposed planning methodology is demonstrated via a case study on an Indian military station for the period of next seven years. The coordinated charging schemes are found to significantly reduce the upgrade cost in this particular case study.

articleTitle: Development and Experimental Validation of a Proportional Resonant Controller for Single-Phase PFC Rectifier with Active Power Decoupling
abstract: Single-phase power factor correction (PFC) rectifier consists of two components of input power namely DC output power and ripple power with double-line frequency. Aluminium electrolytic capacitors (AECs) are usually connected at DC-link to minimize these inherent ripple power components. However, these AECs may not handle as much ripple current per unit of stored energy. Therefore, to get higher power density and efficiency, active power decoupling (APD) is an effective way to replace these bulky AECs with smaller capacitors. Since the APD involves additional semiconductor switches, it introduces power losses that affect the efficiency of the converter. Adding an auxiliary branch, which comprises an inductor and a diode, to the single-phase PFC with APD can achieve zero voltage switching (ZVS) and improve the efficiency of the converter. With the limitation of a proportional-integral (PI) controller for the decoupling inductor current which is flowing at twice the grid frequency, a discrete proportional resonant (PR) controller has been proposed in the current control loop of a decoupling inductor. The proposed PR controller has been validated using simulations performed in MATLAB/SIMULINK and experiments carried out with the SYNDEM smart grid research and educational kit/hardware. Simulations and experimental validation results revealed the effectiveness of the proposed PR controller in tracking the reference values of DC output voltage and decoupling capacitor voltage under steady-state and transient operating conditions.

articleTitle: Smart Charging Station Infrastructure: A Data-Driven Approach to EV Charging Station Management
abstract: Our research at IIT Hyderabad leveraged smart meter data to investigate electric vehicle (EV) energy consumption and charging preferences. In March 2023, we recorded 1660.56 kWh of EV energy consumption, resulting in costs of Rs. 15,775.32 under the regular tariff and Rs. 11,734.41 under the Time-of-Day (TOD) tariff. Our analysis revealed peak charging hours during mid-peak and off-peak periods, with Wednesdays and Thursdays being the busiest days. The TOD tariff showed a significant cost saving of Rs. 4,040.91 compared to the regular tariff. Additionally, we found that solar implementation can reduce the charging station owner's monthly bill by 30 % and save 872.98 tons of emissions. Our study highlights the importance of smart metering infrastructure, data analytics, and scheduling in optimizing EV charging station operations and reducing costs. By leveraging scheduling strategies, EV infrastructure planners can further maximize profits and contribute to a more sustainable and efficient energy ecosystem.

articleTitle: An Energy Operator Based High Impedance Fault Detection Scheme
abstract: Distribution systems frequently encounter high-impedance faults when a live conductor contacts a high-impedance surface. Conventional ground protection methods, which depend on the magnitude of the ground current, may fail to detect these faults due to the low fault current magnitude. A high impedance ground fault protection technique based on time-domain analysis has been developed for TT and TN-S grounded low voltage distribution systems. This method detects ground faults by estimating a fault detection index (FDI) derived from the teager energy content in filtered ground current. The filtered ground current is extracted using a Butterworth filter. The proposed method was validated in a low-voltage distribution system using PSCAD simulation for various faults and non-fault scenarios. Additionally, the method performance is verified using high-resistance fault data obtained from a hardware setup implemented in the laboratory. Both simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the technique accurately identifies high-impedance ground faults in low-voltage distribution systems.

articleTitle: Investigation of New Oscillatory Phenomena in a Multi-Machine Power System Embedding VSG-Controlled PV Plants
abstract: The large integration of inertia-less renewable energy sources (RESs), such as solar photovoltaic (PV) systems, leads to several stability challenges in the electrical grid. The virtual synchronous generator (VSG) has emerged as a promising technology for dealing with such stability challenges. It enables the RES to behave like a conventional synchronous generator. Therefore, it becomes crucial to identify the impact of VSGs when employed with inertia-less RES in large power systems. In this paper, the impact of VSGs is assessed when they are employed with PV plants in a multi-machine power system. For the purpose of analysis, both the higher-order subtransient and lower-order one-axis VSG models are chosen. The assessment is performed by means of both frequency domain and time domain analyses after replacing several conventional generators with VSG-controlled PV plants. The studies have been carried out on the IEEE 68-bus 16-machine power system on the MATLAB/Simulink platform.

articleTitle: Phase Network Decomposition for Fault Analysis Without Symmetrical Components
abstract: Symmetrical component method has been used in calculation of fault currents required for relay settings, and, also for assessing its impact on power transfer capacities (open-conductor faults) in power networks. Along with the component transformation, sequence networks are required which are differently interconnected for different types of faults. More often the analysis is conducted for setting of protective relays. A new method of phase-network decomposition (PND) is proposed here which can be used both for protection and for assessments of power transfer impacts in radial and meshed networks. A current-squared variable is used with end-to-end power-paths instead of the phasor current loops. PND is not transformation-based. It works with actual currents and actual network. Thumb-rules can be derived in terms of the network-parameters. A measure of unbalance can be obtained. Theory of symmetrical components has lived a graceful life for more than a century. With utmost respect to the theory, power professionals may like to examine this new method for its simplicity.

articleTitle: Controller Hardware in Loop Implementation of Unified Virtual Oscillator with Improved Frequency Droop
abstract: Unified Virtual Oscillator Control (uVOC) is a decentralized control strategy used in power systems to manage inverter-based resources. In grid forming (GFM) converter operation, non-linear droop relations of uVOC require setpoints for active and reactive power to be close to the operating point. Determining setpoints for GFM converters operating in islanded mode under varying load conditions is challenging, and the absence of setpoints can cause increased frequency deviations. To address this issue, a reactive power-dependent non-linear frequency droop is proposed that minimizes frequency deviation and nearly restores the frequency to its nominal value without using any setpoints. Additionally, the proposed modification makes virtual impedance more effective in enhancing reactive power sharing among Distributed Generations (DG). Although there is a slight deviation in active power sharing under highly inductive load conditions, the reactive power sharing remains proportionate. Extensive simulations and controller hardware-in-loop (CHIL) results validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Electricity Trading for Offshore Wind Energy Projects in India
abstract: Offshore wind (OFW) can significantly contribute to India's energy transition, especially in light of the country's goal to achieve 500 GW of renewable energy capacity across various technologies by 2030. The National Institute of Wind Energy (NIWE) has identified a potential of about 70 GW that is spread across the eight zones each of the coasts of Gujarat and Tamil Nadu for offshore wind farm development in India. This paper aims to analyze the power offtake options for an upcoming offshore wind farm in Tamil Nadu. In India, the various tariff structures for renewable power include long-term and short-term Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs), open access and market segments like the Green Day Ahead Market (GDAM) and Green Term Ahead Market (GTAM). Among these options for offshore wind power, GDAM, GTAM and long-term PPAs are considered in this paper. Simulations are carried out with the wind speed taken from ERA5 climate data for the site ‘subzone 2’ of Tamil Nadu, and a comparison of the revenues generated from various trading options are presented.

articleTitle: PV - Energy Storage Based EV Charging Infrastructure: Performance Analysis
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of novel photovoltaic (PV) electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure by integrating solar energy with an energy storage system (ESS) interfaced with the grid. In situations of the unpredictable nature of solar power generation, the ESS plays a vital role in maintaining uninterrupted charging by providing power during low PV output and also storing excess energy during periods of high solar generation. The integration of the AC grid not only serves as a backup to guarantee continuous charging even when solar and ESS resources are insufficient but also acts as a power balancing mechanism dynamically. The paper demonstrates the system's effectiveness in maintaining constant voltage-constant current (CV-CC) for EV charging under four distinct operating modes of operation by way of modeling components in a PSCAD environment. This paper contributes to the development of a sustainable PV-based EV charging infrastructure with reduced stress on the AC grid thus enhancing operational flexibility for EV charging at large.

articleTitle: Knowledge Inference Concept of Control Sharing - Mitigation of Power Quality Disturbances in Grid Tied PV Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a pioneering approach to developing a Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC) for grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) systems, combining distributed generation with active power filtering. We revolutionize the field by employing advanced control strategies, including the Synchronous Reference Frame (SRF) theory integrated with sliding mode control for rapid adaptation to voltage sags and swells, and a cutting-edge Artificial Neural Network (ANN) algorithm designed to enhance cost-efficiency. MATLAB/Simulink simulations are conducted to evaluate total harmonic distortion (THD) in both load and grid voltage/current across varying conditions, alongside system response times and performance under unbalanced loads. This research introduces a breakthrough control-sharing method to address extreme voltage sag and swell in grid-tied PV systems. By integrating two UPQCs into the system, this pioneering strategy leverages a knowledge-based framework that adjusts operational parameters based on the severity of voltage fluctuations. The primary UPQC, driven by sliding mode control, handles moderate sag and swell conditions, while the secondary UPQC activates during more severe instances. Results demonstrate a significant enhancement in system performance, particularly under nonlinear and unbalanced load scenarios, proving this dual-UPQC configuration to be far superior to traditional single-UPQC systems in grid-tied PV applications.

articleTitle: Integrating NCMRWF Numerical Weather Model for Improved Solar and Wind Power Forecast in Southern Region REMC
abstract: Given the large-scale integration of renewable energy into India's power system, the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (CERC) has focused on the forecasting, scheduling, and accounting of these energy sources at inter-state level. To support the planned integration of 500 GW of renewable energy into the Indian electrical grid, the Commission introduced regulatory provisions and an implementation framework. Considering the variable nature of renewable energy generation and its impact on the interstate grid, accurate forecasting and scheduling of power have been prioritized. Regional Renewable Energy Management Centres (REMC) adhere to uniform practices for integrating renewable energy, ensuring its visibility, forecasting, and scheduling. Forecasting is crucial for the efficient dispatch of renewable energy generation by Regional Load Dispatch Centres. Wind and solar generating stations can use day-ahead or intra-day forecast from Regional Renewable Energy Management Centres (REMCs) for scheduling purposes, in accordance with CERC regulations. This paper discusses the performance of Internal Forecasting Tool (IFT) of SRLDC REMC system using weather forecast data from National Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasting (NCMRWF) an indigenous organization, its challenges & scope of improvement.

articleTitle: Case Study on Interchangeability Challenges of Siprotec-5 BCUs with Varying Product Codes: Experience with POWERGRID Kishanganj Substation, India
abstract: Bay control units (BCUs) are state-of-the-art devices used in Electrical power system for integrating protection, control, measurement and automation functions. Though BCUs of various reputed manufacturers (Siemens, ABB, GE) are available; in this paper the latest offering from Siemens, the Siprotec-5 BCU has been discussed. Despite their advanced functional and cybersecurity features, recent incidents have highlighted high failure rates of these BCUs and complex maintenance challenges. This paper discusses the architecture of SIPROTEC 5 BCUs and innovative problem-solving techniques involved in making a BCU with different product code compatible for one-to-one replacement with a BCU having another product code. The paper provides recommendations about how to change the product code of a Siprotec-5 BCU to any other product code, for one-to-one replacement with a faulty BCU in the event of unavailability of spare. The case study mentioned in this paper would benefit a lot of power system engineers in resolving some of the major issues encountered with the Siprotec-5 BCUs and ensuring proper monitoring and control of the power system elements.

articleTitle: Modeling and Impact Analysis of e-Bus Chargers
abstract: India has set ambitious goals for electrification of public transportation. Electric buses are slowly replacing fuel-based ones as an eco-friendly alternative. Given the significant charging needs of e-Buses, there is a nationwide initiative to establish public charging stations equipped with high-capacity chargers rated at 150 kW and beyond. EV chargers, being non-linear loads, pose a threat of increased harmonics into the distribution grid, resulting in a negative impact on asset lifespan. A better understanding of the impact of high-capacity EV Chargers may assist utilities in better designing of the distribution systems. Under the research work reported in this paper, power quality related data was collected from a major electric bus charging depot in Bangalore, India. Based on the collected data, simulation models of 240 kW EVSEs have been developed in MATLAB Simulink environment and the effect of such EV Chargers on the distribution system is analyzed.

articleTitle: Power Sharing and Harmonic Compensation in Islanded AC Microgrid Using Complex Impedance-Based Droop Controller
abstract: In an islanded AC microgrid, a conventional droop controller is commonly employed in a decentralized manner to facilitate active and reactive power allocation among the Distributed Generation units (DGs). While P-f droop controllers effectively regulate active power sharing, the Q-V droop exhibits notable inaccuracies in reactive power sharing primarily due to a mismatch in the feeder impedance and variation in local demand. This paper aims to regulate active and reactive power among the DGs accurately and compensate for the harmonics. This is achieved by employing a complex impedance-based droop control along with virtual impedance. A multi-resonant voltage and current controllers are implemented in a decentralized manner to achieve accurate fundamental and harmonic power sharing. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated with the simulation results of an AC microgrid system with two DGs and it is found that reactive power sharing error is reduced from 72.51 % to 20% in passive load scenario. Also, the voltage THD is reduced from 6.64% to 3.08% in case of active load.

articleTitle: Designing, Testing and Implementation of System Protection Schemes (SPS) in Assam Power System as a First Line of Defense Against Constraints in Transmission System Elements
abstract: Maintaining system reliability is one of the foremost concerns of any transmission sector utility. Certain constraints in the transmission system elements e.g. lack of N-1 redundancy in power system elements, constraints in loading capabilities of transmission lines, transformers, etc. may lead to undesired system conditions where the stability of a wide area of the transmission system network may be at stake. The modern IEC 61850 compliant IEDs (Intelligent Electronic Devices) can perform fast, accurate and extensive logical decisions with respect to prevailing system conditions. The capability of the IEDs can be extensively used to design wide area SPS (System Protection Schemes) to protect and preserve the reliability, security, and integrity of the grid during abnormal system conditions. The following paper describes the designing, testing and implementation of various SPS in the Assam power system network which have proved to be successful in preserving the stability of the grid. The SPS has been designed utilizing the present protection and communication system of AEGCL (Assam Electricity Grid Corporation Limited) with a primary focus on reduction in additional hard wirings, reduction in additional cost involvement, efficient use of IEC 61850 features of the IEDs and designing a fail proof scheme with efficient control and monitoring features

articleTitle: High Frequency Power Transformer Design for Isolated Power Supplies
abstract: This paper provides a simple mathematical program to design high frequency transformer usually presented in isolated power supplies. A systematic procedure is available in the literature to design high frequency transformer for isolated power supplies. It is believed to be a novel contribution to develop program using commercial software so that physical burden can be reduced. The proposed idea computationally programmed using MATLAB environment. The proposed program is extensively tested to provide design of high frequency power transformer of various isolated power supplies.

articleTitle: Analysis of P2P Energy Sharing Considering the Energy and Revenue Loss to Utility
abstract: This study investigates the economic and technical impacts of peer-to-peer (P2P) energy sharing within utility sectors, focusing on utility revenue dynamics and energy distribution outcomes in the context of renewable energy sources (RES) such as solar photovoltaics (PV) and wind. It aligns with India's ambitious renewable energy targets and global net-zero emissions objectives, emphasizing the importance of expanding rooftop solar installations. Three scenarios are analyzed: Case 1 establishes baseline utility losses and revenue with a network comprising 350 consumers and 50 prosumers under a three-phase unbalanced distribution network. Case 2 demonstrates a 14.1% reduction in network losses and a 24.5% revenue decrease due to customer-sited generation under net metering, while Case 3 reveals nuanced revenue dynamics with a 36.9% decrease compared to Case 1 and a 19.4% decrease compared to Case 2 when integrating PV with P2P sharing. Real-world data and OpenDSS simulations model various scenarios to quantify the financial implications of P2P trading within utility networks. This research enhances understanding of decentralized energy systems' impacts on utility revenue models, providing valuable insights for policymakers and stakeholders on the economic viability and technical challenges of integrating renewable energy and P2P trading into utility networks.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Battery Energy Storage System in Renewable Integrated Distribution Network Using Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Arithmetic Optimization Algorithm (AOA) has been used in this paper to address the optimal scheduling with placement and sizing of battery energy storage systems (BESS) in renewable integrated electrical distribution system. The objective is to minimize the total system cost which includes cost incurred due to BESS capital and operation & maintenance (O&M), power losses, peak demand and voltage regulation. The charging and discharging of battery is considered to be periodic for the considered interval i.e., 24 hour period and is represented using fourier series. To validate the algorithm, the IEEE 33 node distribution network is considered as test network. The results reveal that the day ahead scheduling of BESS with optimal size and location is helpful to reduce the power losses, voltage deviation, peak demand and total system cost of the test system.

articleTitle: Conditions for Failure of Numerical Estimation of Decaying DC Component in Fault Current
abstract: The estimation of the Decaying DC component (DDC) in fault currents plays a key role in the electrical protection of the power network. Several methods have been proposed in the literature for the estimation of DDC parameters, viz., the peak magnitude and decay rate E. These methods can be broadly categorized as: methods that filter DDC (category-I) and methods that numerically estimate DDC (category-II). However, even today, the industry prefers mimic and cosine filters (category-I methods) for network protection. This paper presents the first in-depth mathematical analysis and associated conditions for which category-II methods may fail to provide valid numeric estimates of E. This analysis is also supported by several numeric results for fault currents in the presence of Gaussian noise.

articleTitle: Application of Impedance Matching Method for Fault Location Identification on Series Compensated Transmission Line
abstract: This paper presents an application of proposed impedance matching algorithm for fault location identification method on series compensated lines. The proposed method is independent of transmission line parameters accuracy. The +ve sequence impedance calculated using pre-fault and during the fault values are compared for fault location identification. The MOV is also considered for overvoltage protection of the series capacitor. Depending on the fault current value, the fault location can be estimated from the two procedures developed and then the section on which fault occurs. The proposed impedance matching method is not dependant on fault resistance and is giving accurate results for various faults at different fault sections and locations. A two terminal network is considered for simulation studies which are modelled in PSCAD® software and the algorithm for fault location is implemented in MATLAB®.

Author Keywords: Prefault and during fault voltage and current phasors

articleTitle: Enhanced Stability in Virtual Synchronous Machines Through Improved Damping Utilizing Parameter Estimation
abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources (RES) into traditional power systems, enabled by advancements in power electronic converters, has posed challenges for grid stability, such as reduced inertia and protection coordination issues. To address these, virtual synchronous machines (VSM) have emerged as a solution, enhancing system stability by emulating a synchronous machine (SM) model in the control converter interface. A key factor affecting stability is the emulation of damping, particularly the damping factor. This paper proposes an effective damping method to enhance the VSM response through parameter optimization. Results show superior dynamic response with variable control, reducing settling time, peak overshoot and oscillations of power supplied by the inverter. The paper offers a comprehensive analysis, including mathematical modeling of the SM and VSM, and a comparative simulation using parameter optimization techniques.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Impact of EVPL and DER on Contemporary Distribution System
abstract: The surge in electric transportation is getting attentions with growing concerns in surrounding environmental degradation and escalating energy consumption, alongside significant advancements in battery technology. As electric vehicles (EVs) gain widespread acceptance, it is evident that their charging demands will poses challenges to the operational dynamics of the power grid. EVs will charge either at home or parking lots with medium charging levels on account of its several socio-techno-economic advantages. However, the large-scale integration of these charging facilities may lead to the issues related to voltage instability, reduced reserve margins, higher peak load demand, and reliability on the grid. The purpose of this work is to examine how the loads from commercial EV parking lot affect voltage stability and power losses in distribution network and to obtain its optimum location. In this work, the optimal location of the parking lot has been determined based on peak power losses and voltage profile deviation over the 24 hours in the system. The impact of the rooftop solar photovoltaic (SPV) is also examined on the obtained optimal located parking lot. The results indicates that power purchasing cost is reduced by 35.6 % with using 63.21% solar power of the total energy consumption over a day. The simulations have been made on the standard 33 bus test bench distribution system.

articleTitle: Guardians of Grid Resilience: Real-World Lessons from Digital Relay Data in Indian Power Sector
abstract: Digital microprocessor-based relays are being used across all substations of POWERGRID. An intrinsic benefit of employing digital relays lies in the substantial volume of data they furnish for post-fault analysis. The amalgamation of disturbance reports from digital relays and the sequence of events extracted from the SCADA system, when meticulously analyzed, yields invaluable insights. This comprehensive analysis aids utilities in identifying major relay setting issues, wiring problems, configuration errors, or relay card failures. The insights derived from disturbance reports and sequence of event play a pivotal role in avoiding protection mis-operations during system disturbances, thereby improving the reliability of the overall system. This paper delves into real-world case studies from the Indian power sector to elucidate how relay events and disturbance reports facilitate utilities in circumventing protection system mis-operations. The discussion encompasses scenarios related to bus bar protection relays, reactor differential relays, and transformer backup protection relays. The paper highlights challenges and opportunities for protection engineers in terms of analysis of relay data for improving the system reliability by avoiding protection system mis-operation. This paper aspires to serve as a reference for utility protection engineers, offering insights into the analysis of disturbance reports, events, and analog data from digital relays and SCADA systems. The multitude of case studies presented herein aims to empower readers to proactively address potential protection mis-operations at their substations, making informed decisions based on the available data.

articleTitle: Dynamic Analysis of Grid Connected Multi-PMBLDC Motor System Under Power-Stage and Hall Sensor Faults
abstract: A Permanent Magnet Brushless Direct current (PMBLDC) is being used vividly in various industrial applications, like in power generation, steel production, vacuum pumps, textile industry, electric vehicles (as a multi-motor in-wheel drive system), etc. Despite its low-maintenance nature, the motor is susceptible to a variety of faults when operated continuously. Consequently, the motors that are not affected by these faults may be impacted when a multiple-machine system is used for a specific application and is connected to a common DC grid. This paper aims to model and evaluate the impact of switch short circuit and open-circuit faults of inverter and hall faults on one of the BLDC motors, as well as on the other motor connected to the same DC grid. The overall system under this study has two PMBLDC motor drives that are connected to a common DC bus system which is further connected to the AC grid. The voltage source inverter (VSI) and Hall sensor faults are simulated and their impact on the dynamics of electrical and mechanical parameters like speed, stator current, back-emf, and torque are observed and analyzed. The analysis is carried out in the MATLAB Simulink platform.

articleTitle: Online Conformal Prediction of Battery Capacity Fade from Partial Charging/Discharging Profiles
abstract: Accurate estimation of battery capacity fade during operation is crucial for timely re-purposing and optimised usage. Non-invasive methods such as Incremental Capacity Analysis (ICA) can be combined with machine learning to estimate capacity fade online from externally measurable signals without damaging the battery. Current methods in the literature typically utilise multiple features of ICA curves obtained during a full charge/discharge cycle, making them unsuitable for applications like Battery Energy Storage Systems that may encounter partial charging/discharging cycles while providing grid services. In this paper, we propose a Gaussian Process Regression-based conformal prediction model for estimating the capacity fade of a cell based on ICA. By considering the state-of-charge range, this method provides accurate capacity fade estimates with realistic prediction intervals, even when the cell is partially charging/discharging. The efficacy of the proposed method is confirmed by simulations performed on a validated dynamic model of a commercial cell in the presence of output noise.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Overvoltages in Shunt Compensated Transmission Lines of Indian National Grid During Single Pole Autoreclose Considering Secondary Arc Model in PSCAD
abstract: Shunt reactors are mainly deployed in long high voltage transmission systems to absorb excessive reactive power and to improve the energy transfer capability. They are also used for enhancing the stability of the system by maintaining the voltage profile of the power system. Shunt compensation is a robust technique to improve system loadability and voltage profile of EHV lines, however under overcompensated conditions the same may cause over voltage during single pole auto-reclose (SPAR) operation. Secondary arc current is high during some specific overcompensated condition and auto reclose operation may not be successful. Also, the same may cause tripping of lines on operation of overvoltage stage-2 protection during the dead time. In general, Neutral Grounding Reactors (NGRs) are used with Line reactors for suppressing this secondary arching phenomenon. However, in the absence of NGRs or with NGR of lower ratings, during dead time of auto reclose, problem of Secondary arcing and resonance overvoltage have been observed in overcompensated lines. Overvoltage tripping during resonance conditions causes threat to secured system operation. In this paper, PSCAD simulation performed considering secondary arcing model for mitigation of resonance overvoltage in overcompensated transmission lines is presented with a real case study in National Grid of India.

articleTitle: Optimizing Fairness in Peer-to-Peer Energy Systems for Effective Duck Curve Management
abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources, particularly solar, has introduced challenges such as the duck curve phenomenon in energy grids, characterized by midday surplus and evening peaks in demand. This paper proposes an optimization model for peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading systems aimed at mitigating the duck curve while ensuring fair energy distribution among participants. The model formulates an objective function that minimizes deviations from a target load profile, emphasizing both load flattening and equitable energy sharing. Constraints include energy balance equations, storage limits, and trading bounds, ensuring operational feasibility. MATLAB simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in achieving significant reductions in peak loads and promoting fairness in energy transactions. By optimizing energy trades based on participant preferences and system-wide objectives, the proposed approach seeks to enhance grid stability and efficiency in decentralized energy markets.

articleTitle: Implementation of IoT Enabled DC Home Appliances Scheduling and Control
abstract: IoT (Internet of Things) has revolutionized the way we interact with technology and appliances in our daily lives. The main objective of this paper is to develop a Home Energy Management System (HEMS) that allows the user to schedule and control their Direct Current (DC) home appliances using IoT technology. The system will enable the user to monitor the energy usage of their appliances, control them remotely, and schedule them to turn on and off at specific times. This system will save energy, reduce their electricity bills, and reduce Peak to Average Ratio (PAR). The key components of this implementation include sensing and control unit along with microcontrollers to optimize scheduling algorithm, a web application to monitor energy consumption and cloud storage to store and retrieve data. The proposed system was implemented and tested on a prototype setup, and its performance was evaluated. The results demonstrate that the system effectively optimizes energy consumption while maintaining the PAR as well. The system also provides real-time feedback to users on their energy consumption patterns and enables them to make informed decisions on energy usage. The implementation of an IoT-enabled DC home appliances scheduling, and control system offers users the convenience, flexibility, and energy savings, making it a valuable addition to modern smart homes.

articleTitle: Power Management and Control of a PV-Hydro-Biomass-Battery-Based Standalone DC Microgrid
abstract: Renewable sources like PV, wind, hydro, and biomass energy are vital in today's generation system for mitigating environmental pollution. Hybridization is encouraged because of the intermittent nature of these non-conventional energy sources. Load demand satisfaction and power management are ensured by the battery management system (BMS). BMS also ensures maintaining DC link voltage and charging-discharging cycles of the battery. More than two renewable sources are considered for a more reliable and robust system. The analysis is done at various dynamic changes in the system. The behavioral changes in energy sources with respect to load and storage systems is observed. The overarching goal is to investigate and evaluate various technical aspects of hybrid renewable energy storage system (HRESS), encompassing system architectures, modeling approaches, power conversion strategies, and optimization methodologies, to facilitate the effective integration and operation of multiple renewable energy sources and energy storage technologies within a unified hybrid system.

articleTitle: Fault Analysis of Inverter-Interfaced Grid Connected Photovoltaic Systems Using Wavelet Transformation
abstract: This paper proposes a modern technique for fault detection and classification in the transmission lines connecting the power grid integrating with inverter-based resources (IBRs) by the implementation of the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT). This wavelet transform releases the wavelet coefficient energy when some disturbance occurs in the system and it provides a high speed fault detection. Protection of transmission lines containing IBRs using this technique greatly enhance the reliability of the system. To validate the proposed technique, a model is developed consisting Photovoltaic (PV) arrays, doublestage converter, transmission line and power grid. Also, faults of various types are simulated randomly on the developed model using MATLAB/Simulink software (2021b).

articleTitle: One Sided Impedance Base Fault Location Algorithm for Multi Tap Distribution Systems
abstract: Accurate fault location identification in distribution systems (DS) is crucial for rapid system restoration. The complexity of fault detection increases due to the numerous branches present in DS. This paper presents an impedance-based method for precise fault location estimation using the fundamental phasor components of current and voltage measured only at the substation. The single-ended measurement approach reduces the need for additional meters. The method utilizes both pre-fault and during-fault currents to compute the superimposed pure-fault current, which is then employed to determine the equivalent impedance as observed from the substation. This equivalent impedance accurately indicates the fault location. MATLAB simulations validate the approach by testing different fault types like three-phase, two-phase, and single-phase to ground at various points in a multi tap feeder configuration.

articleTitle: Prediction of Heating and Cooling Load Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Accurate prediction models for heating and cooling loads are essential for enhancing building energy efficiency, a key component of sustainable development. This study evaluates the effectiveness of three regression methods-Linear Regression, Random Forest Regression, and Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers-based Regression-in predicting these loads. The dataset comprises various building parameters, with heating and cooling loads as target variables. We aim to identify the most accurate and robust predictive model for load forecasting in buildings. Linear Regression was used as the baseline model and is a widely applied method for forecasting. Random Forest Regression is an ensemble learning approach that has been applied to a number of forecasting problems. It averages predictions from multiple decision trees and is, therefore, able to capture nonlinear relationships in the most accurate ways. BERT-based Regression, though initially designed for natural language processing tasks, has also been utilized to solve some forecasting problems. Its capability to handle large datasets and complex relationships furthers its case in prediction applications. The results underscore Random Forest Regression as the most effective method for predicting building energy loads. This study utilized Python and its various machine-learning libraries to implement and compare the above methods.

articleTitle: Synchrophasor Signature Analysis for Real Time Grid Operation
abstract: Synchro phasors play a crucial role in post-dispatch analysis, providing valuable insights of the dynamic behavior of the grid during grid disturbances through unique signatures. The visualization and analysis of these signatures enable deep understanding and facilitate secure and faster power system restoration. This paper presents various case studies demonstrating the efficacy of WAMS and PMU signatures in a meshed grid, highlighting how PMU applications have aided grid operators in restoration and identifying various fault natures, protection coordination discrepancies via signature analysis. The paper also highlights the increased visibility and observability of the grid with availability of PMU data.

articleTitle: Operational Analysis of a Major Blackout of Generating Station Due to Breaker Flashover in Southern Region of India and Key Improvements for Resilience
abstract: Breaker flashover incidents present a formidable challenge within electrical systems, often resulting in prolonged fault feeding and potential vulnerabilities in existing protection mechanisms. The absence of dedicated protection systems specifically designed to address breaker flashover events creates a critical safety gap in system operations. The implementation of specialized protection solutions capable of swiftly detecting and isolating breaker flashover occurrences holds the potential to significantly enhance the reliability and safety of electrical systems. This paper conducts a comprehensive operational analysis of a significant blackout experienced at a generating station in the Southern Region of India. The blackout occurred as a result of a breaker flashover during the synchronization of the generator with the grid. The flashover triggered a series fault in the R-phase of the breaker, consequently generating a neutral current within neighboring equipment. Due to non-availability of a dedicated Breaker Flashover scheme in the generating station, the flashover was identified solely by the directional earth fault protection at the remote ends of the feeders connected to the station, eventually being cleared after approximately 4 seconds. This paper also includes simulation study of similar scenarios using PSCAD underscoring the imperative need for a tailored breaker flashover protection scheme to proactively avert similar incidents in the future. By exploring the intricacies of the event and its ramifications, this paper aims to deepen the understanding of breaker flashover incidents and advocate for the advancement of protection strategies in both power generation and transmission systems.

articleTitle: Short-Term Load Forecasting for Indian Railways Using Seasonal-Trend Decomposition
abstract: In this paper, we propose a model for forecasting railway loads, which is essential for the efficient operation and power management of Indian Railways. However, the task is challenging due to the inherent time series randomness in Indian railway load data. This randomness can lead to inaccuracies in model training, affecting the quality of predictions. To address this, we decomposed the time series data into trend, seasonal, and residual components by using STL decomposition. To predict the trend, we use the SARIMA model, which is well-suited for capturing trend patterns. For modeling the seasonality and residual components, we employ the FBprophet model, which excels at handling seasonal patterns. By combining the strengths of ARIMA and FBprophet, we aim to improve the accuracy of our load forecasting model. The Comparison is done with the proposed model and the major existing techniques, we observed significant reductions in Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) for each state. This indicates that our proposed model is effective in handling the uncertain load patterns of Indian Railways. As a result, it presents a suitable solution for achieving accurate short-term load forecasting in the railway system.

articleTitle: Power Network Twin Framework as Enabler for Advanced System Studies and Diagnostics
abstract: A framework for power network twin suitable for advanced power system studies and diagnostics is presented in this paper. The framework is developed with Python and uses data coming from IEC61850 enabled intelligent electronic devices to keep itself updated in real time. A substation level power network twin is presented as a proof of concept, showing parameter updates in a graphical user interface along with a diagnostic use case for machine learning based transformer dissolved gas analysis. Unlike a SCADA system, the power network twin framework developed can be leveraged for analyzing past performance, simulating contingencies, deploying complex diagnostic algorithm, conducting accelerated aging studies and many more.

articleTitle: Flexibility Requirement and Resource Adequacy in a Distribution Company
abstract: This paper discusses the flexibility requirements in view of increasing renewable integration and existing resource adequacy regulatory guidelines in India. It demonstrates various flexibilization efforts being taken at Tata Power Mumbai, to ensure uninterrupted supply to its consumers maintaining grid parameters. This paper also discusses the probable challenges may be faced by power utilities in complying to regulations and suggest ways to improve flexibility and resource adequacy compliances. The study indicates that capacity additions required, to comply resource adequacy requirements, may have severe financial impact on end consumers.

articleTitle: TPS Control-Based Current Stress Reduction for Dual Active Bridge Converters
abstract: The Dual Active Bridge (DAB) converter is a versatile and widely used power electronics topology that offers high efficiency and voltage conversion capabilities in various applications like EV fast charging. However, optimizing its current stress and improving its overall efficiency remains ongoing challenge due to the circulating current. The objective of this research is to develop a control scheme that optimizes the current stress distribution across the DAB converter components while improving its efficiency. This is addressed by leveraging the Triple Phase Shift (TPS) control with optimized control parameters. It has the capability to intelligently manage the power flow with reduced current stress on the critical components of the converter. The comprehensive mathematical model of DAB converter with TPS control working in forward buck mode is presented and then the optimal phase shift that minimize the current stress is derived. The performance of this model is evaluated under different operating and loading conditions. The effectiveness of the optimized TPS control is validated through the simulations and compared with non-optimized TPS control.

articleTitle: Smart Meter Data Analytics for Residential Consumers
abstract: According to data on Indian household consumption, air conditioners (AC) and water heaters (WH) are the main contributors to the high peak demand in residential houses. To study the consumption behavior of these appliances, smart meter data from Pune households with AC and WH ownership is analyzed to extract attributes corresponding to AC and WH usage. Specifically, peak events are observed and their attributes are analyzed. These attributes facilitate understanding of the usage of AC and WH appliances and the associated behavioral patterns. To enrich the limited dataset, a synthetic dataset generation algorithm is proposed: it constructs household profiles by using suitable randomization on peak event attributes, thereby capturing consumption behaviors similar to real households. Statistical metrics indicate that the generated profiles closely resemble real household behavior, although their monthly average power consumption profile differs. Synthetic households provide a rich and diverse dataset for academia and electric utilities to study demand response and demand side management scenarios.

articleTitle: Classification of Complex Power Quality Disturbances Using Wavelet Scalogram and Computer Vision Approach
abstract: Power quality problems are increasing many folds due to transformations of smart distribution grid and penetration of renewable energy sources. Power quality issues deteriorate the performance of the systems and lead to techno-economic losses. To detect and classify the signals and its anomalies, signal processing techniques along with artificial intelligence is becoming a promising tool. Therefore, this work focuses on the application of wavelet transform and computer vision for classification of power quality disturbances. In this work, wavelet scalograms are generated from the disturbance signals using wavelet transform to extract time-frequency characteristics. Wavelet scalograms, represented as 2-D images, are utilized to evaluate the effectiveness of MobileNetV2 pre-trained CNN models in both training and testing phases. From the results, it can be perceived that the proposed approach is capable of classifying multiple disturbance signals. To show the superiority of proposed approach, results are compared with the techniques reported in the literature. From the comparative results, it is observed that the proposed method is robust to detect and recognise the power quality disturbances

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Cyber Security Algorithm for Over-Current Relay Setting in Distribution System
abstract: The construction of sophisticated protection schemes for transmission and distribution lines has been made easier by technical advancements in the view of communication and measurement systems. However, the effectiveness and reliability of these schemes are entirely reliant on the integrity, authenticity, and confidentiality of the measured data and control signals transmitted over the underlying relay communication networks. Consequently, leaving targets open to cyberattacks can result in cascade transmission line failures and blackouts. The over-current relays play a crucial role in the distribution system in identifying and isolating faults by maintaining the due time coordination interval between the relays.
