The impact of cyberattacks on the setting of these relays can disrupt power grids, potentially leading to widespread outages. Therefore, this paper proposes blockchain-based frameworks to enhance the security feature of over-current relays against setting tempering/cyberattacks in the distribution system, in which the mined hash code of the secured key and updated setting are compared with the actual hash code. The performance of the proposed approach is tested on a 33-bus distribution system through the MATLAB platform, and results are found to be improved.

articleTitle: Energy Optimization in Smart Microgrid: A Modified Particle Swarm Optimization Approach with Smart Contract
abstract: In recent years, various renewable energy sources along with energy storage systems for power generation have grown significantly due to fossil fuel depletion and increasing environmental concerns. Optimizing energy flow in this system is crucial for efficient resource utilization while adhering to system constraints. Conventional methods for energy optimization include operators or intermediaries which have their own limitations. By using blockchain technology in energy optimization, intermediaries/operators are avoided. Also, its use offers other advantages such as higher security, transparency and immutability of energy transactions. This paper introduces an approach for energy optimization using blockchain in smart microgrid system. A modified algorithm based on new particle swarm optimization (NPSO) is employed for this purpose. The algorithm is executed with the help of smart contract. It schedules, distributed energy sources and determines charging and discharging of energy storage system, while adhering to various system constraints. The algorithm is deployed and tested on a ganache platform which is based on Ethereum. The results obtained from this modified algorithm are compared with the standard PSO algorithm, demonstrating its effectiveness. The study is conducted on a typical smart microgrid system comprising three prosumers, and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Optimal Planning of Hybrid AC/DC Microgrid
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid AC/DC microgrid planning problem is considered. The hybrid grid architecture consists of both AC and DC bus/terminals where a bidirectional converter links these bus interfaces. A cost objective function is formulated considering the variables i.e. maximum installed capacity and binary decision variable to determine the feeder type (AC or DC). The above problem is further subjected to various constraints i.e. power balance constraint and limit constraints. The proposed problem is of non-convex in nature which is convexified and then solved to determine optimum values of the decision variables. In this studied problem consists of a test system including four diesel generator, two non-dispatchable units e.g. solar and wind, and a battery energy storage system. The overall cost is optimized with respective constraints to determine the optimal feeder type and installed capacity. The objective function is solved using CPLEX solver which have the capability to solve mixed integer problems.

articleTitle: Solar Power Smoothing with Batteries of Reduced Size and Improved Life
abstract: Battery energy storage can be used to smooth out short-term fluctuations from solar generation. In practically setting up a such system, the battery nominal energy requirement as well as its deterioration over its lifetime are major contributors to the system cost. An adaptive battery usage strategy is proposed here wherein the battery is used only when required during periods of high variability. Such strategies can significantly reduce the system costs by decreasing the battery size and improving lifetime while maintaining nearly similar levels of smoothing. We use field data to show how the usage of the adaptive operation policy can increase battery life by 64% compared to using the traditional moving average-based smoothing technique for the same battery size and comparable smoothing. Also, a 33% decrease in the battery size is made possible holding the same battery cycle life for the two techniques.

articleTitle: Improving DISCOM Collection Processes with GPS Coordinates
abstract: Collection efficiency, which refers to the effective collection of payments for electricity consumed, is vital for the financial health and operational sustainability of DISCOMS. One of the methods of recovering electricity dues from defaulters (consumers with significant pending electricity dues) is by disconnecting their supply. This is carried out by disconnection gangs, each consisting of one lineman and two helpers, stationed at DISCOM substations. However, the number of defaulters at a substation often exceeds the disconnection capacity of the gang. An inefficient disconnection process at the substation leads to poor recovery of electricity dues from consumers. Improving the disconnection efficiency of the gangs will enhance revenue realization. This paper proposes improving the work efficiency of disconnection gangs, which would result in higher revenue realization and improved collection efficiency. In this paper, we will examine (i) the current list-based methodology of disconnection, (ii) the issues with the present methodology, (iii) the proposed Google My Maps-based disconnection methodology, which is more efficient, and (iv) the calculation of the approximate revenue potential of the My Maps method of disconnection.

articleTitle: Controller Hardware In Loop (C-HIL) Validation of Non-Standard Tripping Characteristics Based Relay Coordination Scheme for Microgrids
abstract: To meet ever-increasing load demand and to re-duce carbon footprints, integration of renewable-based power generation in the form of distributed generation (DGs) gives birth to the concept of microgrids. However numerous challenges needs to be addressed for the successful operation of microgrids including protection coordination issues. The magnitude and fault current direction vary considerably with the varying modes of microgrid operation, which may interfere the coordination among the protective relays present in the microgrids. As directional overcurrent relays are well-suitable for microgrid environments, the adoption of non-standard tripping curves was proposed, which is found to be superior to standard relay characteristics in terms of relay operational time. This work aims for the development of controller hardware in loop setup for validation of the performance of non-standard tripping curve of directional overcurrent relays for microgrid applications using real time digital simulator and typhoon HIL platform ensuring the effectiveness of the proposed protection scheme for real time applications.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Optimization Problem for Load Restoration of Power Distribution Networks by Network Reconfiguration and Repair Crew Deployment
abstract: Extreme events like earthquakes, wildfires, and windstorms are rare but significantly impact power distribution networks (PDNs). Therefore, it is important to improve the resilience of PDNs. Repair crew deployment and network reconfiguration are the two most effective operational measures for the resilience enhancement of PDNs. These two operational measures are utilized in this study for load restoration of PDNs. This study proposes a multi-objective mixed integer linear programming (MO-MILP) model aimed at optimizing the operation of switches and scheduling repair sequences for damaged lines. The optimization problem has two main objectives: the first is to minimize load shedding, and the second is to minimize the cost associated with load restoration. The cost of load restoration includes the operating expenses of switches, as well as the travel and repair expenses of the repair crews. The weighted sum method is used to solve the proposed MO-MILP model. Furthermore, the proposed model is validated using a 33-bus test system.

articleTitle: Simulation Studies of Emergency Transfer System and Load Sequencing in Indian Pressurized Heavy Water Reactor
abstract: Electrical Power Supply System in Indian Pressurized Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) based Nuclear Power Plants consists of Offsite (Grid) power supply and Onsite (Turbo-generator, Diesel Generators, Battery) power supply. Power supply from Grid and/or Turbo-generator is normally used and is called as Preferred Power Supply. On loss of Preferred Power Supply, restoration of power supply to emergency buses from Diesel Generators and sequential load restoration of safety loads is crucial in maintenance of reactor safety. Emergency Transfer System plays a vital role in automatic restoration of power supply and systematic load restoration to avoid tripping of diesel generators on overload. Designing transfer logic by considering all failure scenarios and deciding load sequence to avoid overloading of Diesel Generators are challenging tasks during design stage. Lack of verification of this system during design stage may lead to rework during site testing stages. This paper explains step by step methods and simulations adopted to verify Emergency Transfer & load restoration scheme and to study diesel generator performance during sequential restoration of major loads. Challenges in simulation such as unavailability of motors resistance and reactance values, simulation of dynamic operations of field equipment, modelling of Diesel Generator system are addressed in this paper.

articleTitle: Efficient Compression of PMU Signal Using Ramanujan's Sum Transform
abstract: The Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) forms the basis of a Wide Area Monitoring, Protection, and Control (WAMPAC) system. PMUs capture time-synchronized voltage and current phasors at a higher reporting rate of 50–60 samples per second using Information and Communication Technology (ICT) enabled Global Positioning System (GPS). This results in a significant amount of data that needs to be stored and transmitted for analysis in the control center. Therefore, an efficient PMU data compression scheme is necessary to reduce the cost of storage and the bandwidth required to transmit this data. In this paper, a simple PMU signal compression scheme consisting of 2 modules is proposed. Module 1 separates the event window from the steady state window using Statistical Variance (SV). This results in improved compression and reconstruction performance. Next, Module 2 compresses the separated windows using Ramanujan's Sum Transform (RST) method. The effectiveness of the proposed method is then compared with the conventional Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) for various types of disturbances in the IEEE 14-bus system. Finally, the results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, while future direction is discussed at the end of the paper.

articleTitle: A Harmonic Injection Based Fault Detection Scheme for Inverter Interfaced Islanded Microgrid
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources into microgrids necessitates advanced protection schemes to ensure stability and reliability. Traditional protection methods often face challenges especially in inverter-interfaced islanded microgrids due to limited fault current level. This paper presents a harmonic injection based fault detection scheme for the protection of such microgrids. The scheme addresses the challenge of low fault current level inherent in islanded microgrids by injecting harmonic currents using the inverter control and sensing that current by harmonic relays. The proposed method is validated through extensive simulations considering various fault types and in a wide range of fault resistances, as well as different non-fault transient events. The results indicate that the choice of current limiter significantly impacts harmonic current levels, with different limiters exhibiting varied performance under fault conditions. Additionally, the proposed scheme effectively distinguishes between fault and non-fault conditions, even in the presence of non-linear loads, capacitor switching, and sudden load changes.

articleTitle: Real Time Simulation of Three Phase Bidirectional Onboard Charger for Grid Integration
abstract: The rapid growth of Electrical Vehicles (EVs) in the automotive industry are vital in transition towards a sustainable and carbon neutral future. However use of EVs depends on their charging process and charging infrastructure. The Bidirectional Onboard Chargers (OBC) enable the Bidirectional Power Flow leading to Vehicle to Grid (V2G) and Grid to Vehicle (G2V) modes of operation. The increasing trend of Bidirectional OBCs will impose new challenges to the Power distribution system. So for integration of OBCs into the power distribution system a two stage power converter comprising the three phase two level AC/DC converter and galvanized isolated Dual Active Bridge (DAB) DC/DC converter used. This article exclusively focuses on the detailed modeling of Bidirectional two stage OBCs and their controllers performance is analyzed through the Bode diagrams. A LC filter is analyzed for the different values of the dominant harmonic order output voltages to suppress the ripples present in the converter current and an inductor is used at output of the DAB converter to reduce the ripple current present at the battery. A detailed analysis of the bidirectional OBC is developed and validated in the Real Time Digital Simulator (RTDS) platform.

Author Keywords: Three Phase Two Level AC/DC Converter

articleTitle: Cyber Attack Detection Against State Estimation in CPPS: A Data-Driven Approach
abstract: The amalgamation of Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs), smart sensors and data communication network in the legacy power systems have given rise to a new class of systems called Cyber Physical Power Systems (CPPS). The added complexity in the inter-networking of CPPS, has opened up a broad attack surface, increasing its vulnerability towards cyber attacks. To prevent any potential harm to the system and preserve the integrity of the estimated states, a data-driven, regression based cyber attack detection technique is proposed. A Machine Learning (ML) based State Estimator (SE) is proposed and the predicted system states are compared with the one estimated by the conventional SE to detect any malicious data. Conventional Feed-Forward Deep Neural Network (FFDNN) regression model is compared with Extreme Gradient Boost (XGBoost) in training the historical CPPS measurement data to demonstrate that the later is computationally faster by over three times. The proposed FDIA detection technique is validated on a modified IEEE-33 bus system with the successful detection of the bad data injection strategized by two different approaches.

articleTitle: A Multi-Objective Optimization Model for Smart EV Charging Scheduling Considering the Benefits of EV Owners and Distribution Network Operators
abstract: In this paper, a multi-objective smart charging scheduling scheme is proposed considering both grid-to-vehicle (G2V) and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) operations of electric vehicles (EVs) to benefit two different stakeholders involved in EV-integrated power distribution networks (PDNs). The proposed approach aims to schedule the charging and discharging operations of EVs by simultaneously minimizing the daily charging cost and the peak load demand resulting from EV charging. Minimization of the charging cost benefits the EV owners while flattening the load curve by minimizing the peak load demand benefits the distribution network operators (DNOs). The proposed charging strategy is implemented considering EV charging at the workplace as well as residential charging stations. The effectiveness of the proposed charging scheme is validated on a 33-node distribution network. The multi-objective optimization problem is formulated as a mixed integer linear programming (MILP) model and solved using IBM ILOG CPLEX optimization studio of version 12.10.

articleTitle: Intelligent Auto-Reclosing Protection Scheme for Mixed Transmission Circuits
abstract: Two-terminal mixed transmission circuits are attractive from both environmental and commercial view. Urbanization is leading to an increase in mixed transmission circuits, which connect industrial loads with renewable integration. When mixed lines are involved, auto-reclosing protection becomes more difficult (combined overhead lines with submarine or underground cables). Reclosing following a fault is allowed for sections of overhead lines and disabled for submarine/underground cable sections. We must identify the faulted section to perform the auto-reclosing in mixed circuits. In this paper, an innovative faulted section identification method is proposed using both side voltage and current measurements. Faulted section is identified by checking the sign of the calculated faulted section identification indices. The faulted section identification indices are calculated using the ratio of the difference of voltage and current at each junction of the mixed line. The junction voltage and current are calculated from both terminals using each section parameters and positive sequence voltage and current measurements. The proposed method does not require junction measurements. The method is verified and validated with experimental and field data and results are found to be reliable.

articleTitle: Detection and Mitigation of False Data Injection Attacks in Wide-Area Damping Controller Using Random Forest Classifier
abstract: Modern wide-area power system depends on communication-based operations for monitoring and control and are thus susceptible to cyber-attacks which can undermine the performance of WADC and their stability. Since the input signals for WADC are transmitted to the control location via communication channels, they are also vulnerable to cyber-attacks. An attacker could potentially inject false data to corrupt WADC measurements and control signals. Thus, this study focuses on developing attack models and examining the effects of false data injection (FDI) attacks on WADC performance. Further, a Random forest algorithm-based binary classifier is proposed to detect and classify the FDI-attacked signal from the non-attacked ones. The control framework for assessing such attacks incorporates local power system stabilizers (LPSSs) attached to each generator to mitigate local modes and a residue-based WADC along with the thyristor-controlled series capacitor (TCSC) tasked with damping critical modes within Kundur's test system.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Anomaly Classification of GAN-Generated Catenary Insulators with Self-Supervised DINOv2 Model
abstract: High-speed railway catenary support components, including insulators, are critical for maintaining the contact lines that power trains. However, these components face challenges from environmental conditions, mechanical stress, and high-voltage electrical currents. This can lead to physical damage and compromise the insulation and support provided by the insulators. Although computer vision technology offers effective inspection for detecting insulator defects, automating this process remains challenging due to limited defective samples and subtle defect features. To overcome this problem, this study utilized a public dataset and augmented it using the deep convolutional generative adversarial networks (DCGAN) model, enhancing low-resolution images with the enhanced super-resolution generative adversarial networks (ESRGAN) model for better training. A self-supervised image classifier model was then employed for monitoring insulator conditions, achieving an exceptional 99.57% classification accuracy, outperforming other models. This high accuracy enables proactive maintenance, reducing downtime and enhancing the security and reliability of railway power transmission systems.

articleTitle: Forced Oscillation Source Location Using System Oscillating Energy and Eigensystem Realization Algorithm
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach integrating the Eigen Realisation Algorithm (ERA) with oscillating energy analysis technique to effectively pinpoint the source of forced oscillations (FO). Utilizing ERA, which is a subspace identification method, facilitates the estimation of both frequency and damping ratio of oscillating modes. Modes exhibiting low damping ratios are potentially associated with forced oscillations. These identified modes undergo filtering based on their estimated frequencies. Subsequently, filtered Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) data from the generator terminals are used to calculate the power of oscillating energy fed into the system, facilitating the identification of the forced oscillation source in the system. The proposed approach is validated on wind turbine system (WTS) integrated IEEE 4-machine and 10-machine systems for several test cases, including scenarios when multiple FO sources are present simultaneously in the system.

articleTitle: Techno-Economic Analysis of Coordinated Capacitor and EV Charging Station Placement in Distribution Networks
abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EV) has introduced challenges to distribution networks (DN), including concerns about voltage levels and power losses. Integrating electric vehicle charging stations (EVCS) with capacitors that provide reactive power compensation can help mitigate these issues by improving voltage profiles, minimizing system losses, lowering total energy costs, and reducing interruption costs. This study aims to maximize the net present value (NPV) by reducing energy losses and expected interruption costs (EIC) through the optimal placement of capacitors in DS. Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is employed to identify the best locations for EVCS and capacitors within a DS. Additionally, the study considers the impact of EVCS on NPV and incorporates vehicle-to-grid (V2G) functionality. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated in the IEEE 10-bus system.

articleTitle: Electronic Load Modeling Using Enhanced Opposition Based Differential Evolution Optimization
abstract: Every day, the proportion of electronic loads in a load sector increases. As such, familiarity with and monitoring the electronic load model is crucial. This work addresses the novel challenge of parameter estimation of the electronic load model using enhanced opposition-based differential evolution (EOBDE) optimization. Based on the load terminal voltage value, an electronic load model is created. Electronic load operates in five different modes. Different mathematical models are used for each mode to determine the electronic load's active and reactive power consumption. On the 30th bus, this load is connected to the New England (NE) 39 bus system. Additive white Gaussian noise is applied to the voltage, active power, and reactive power data that are collected. Noises are filtered using the wavelet denoising technique. In light of this, using a measurement-based approach, this filtered data is compared with estimated power output and the error between filtered data and estimated output is fed to the parameter tuning algorithm (EOBDE), and iteratively, by minimizing the error between estimated and filtered output, the parameter of the electronic load is estimated. EOBDE is an improved version of differential evolution optimization that excels in parameter estimation because, when the enhanced opposition section is called, it is based on the opposite of the solution. In the lowest period and with the fewest number of iterations, it minimizes the possibility of local minima and locates the global optimum.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Technique for Hydrogen Fuel Cell Based Microgrid Energy Management
abstract: This study explores the application of reinforcement learning (RL) techniques to the integration of hydrogen fuel cells into microgrids, specifically focusing on the Rye Microgrid in Norway, which operates in island mode.The investigation centers on the seamless integration of fuel cells using reinforcement learning (RL) methods, treating the problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). The state space includes renewable energy production, current energy storage levels, and spot market prices, while the action space involves decisions on charging and discharging energy storage elements. Forecasted state values support the RL agent's decision-making process.A multi-agent RL framework is employed to optimize the actions for both hydrogen fuel cell and battery with the objective of minimizing costs while satisfying energy demand. The study rigorously investigates various RL algorithms, including Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Deep Q-Network (DQN), identifying DQN as the most effective algorithm. Further analysis of the DQN algorithm, considering different forecasting intervals, demonstrates its robustness and adaptability. The study highlights the potential of advanced RL techniques in improving the economic viability and operational efficiency of microgrids incorporating hydrogen fuel cells.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Assessment in Small and Medium-Sized Coir Industry
abstract: An energy audit has been conducted in the coir industry to identify and implement cost-effective strategies for energy reduction. The audit involved both in-depth data analysis and close monitoring of system performance across several pieces of equipment. It revealed numerous potential savings opportunities, particularly for motors, motor pulleys, and ceiling fans. The audit found that inductive loads constitute the majority of the industry's electrical load. This imbalance negatively impacts overall efficiency. To address this, the study suggests raising the power factor to its optimal level. This can be achieved by strategically deploying an Automatic Power Factor Controller (APFC) device. Beyond the power factor, the audit identified two further areas for improvement: under loaded motors and conveyor belt drives. Replacing these underutilized motors with high-efficiency IE3 (+) motors will not only save energy but also significantly reduce costs. Upgrading conveyor belt drives from typical V-belts to cogged belts provides another opportunity for increased efficiency. The focus on energy efficiency extends beyond industrial equipment. The study also suggests replacing existing ceiling fans with energy-efficient BLDC fans. This transition is expected to result in additional energy savings and contribute to a more sustainable operation. Implementing these improvements has a payback period of around 3.5 years, making them an economically viable investment. By implementing these cost-effective measures, the coir industry can achieve a more sustainable future, not only reducing energy consumption but also significantly lowering CO2 emissions.

articleTitle: VSG Based Novel Control for Interlinking Converter in Islanded Hybrid Microgrids
abstract: AC and DC microgrids are joined through interlinking converter in a hybrid microgrid. Control of interlinking converter plays an important part in the overall operation of hybrid microgrid. Whether combining AC and DC microgrids or integrating various renewable energy source to either AC or DC systems, the effect is to add more and more converters to the generation system which are inertia-less. It is a challenge to maintain voltage and frequency stability of such a system during load transients. In this paper, control strategy is formulated for the interlinking converter to make it behave as a synchronous generator. In addition to achieving proportional load sharing, it is able to produce voltage, power support to AC bus during islanding of AC microgrid, feed reactive loads on AC side from DC subgrid and also adds to the inertia of the whole system.

articleTitle: Short-Term Solar PV Generation Forecasting Using Bi-GRU Neural Network
abstract: This study investigates the deep learning-based rolling window approach in forecasting short-term solar PV generation. This study's primary objective is to develop a model for accurate short-term solar power forecasting at high temporal resolution (20-minute intervals). The solar PV generation data obtained from one of the roof-top solar PV systems at IIT Gandhinagar is used to test and validate the forecasting performance of the developed Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (Bi-GRU) neural network based short-term forecast model. This research study contributes valuable insights into adopting deep learning model for solar PV generation forecast and emphasizes the significance of data window size selection in achieving better forecast accuracy. The findings can benefit the development of an improved forecasting model vital for optimizing distributed renewable energy management.

articleTitle: Novel Tuning Strategies to Enhance State Estimator Performance and Quality in the All India Power System Network
abstract: The accuracy and reliability of state estimation are crucial for the effective operation and control of power systems, particularly in large-scale networks. Operators often face challenges such as measurement noise, data redundancy, and computational inefficiencies while striving for optimal solutions. This paper introduces novel tuning strategies to enhance state estimator performance and quality. The paper begins by underscoring the importance of state estimation in power systems. It then examines the integration of SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) and EMS (Energy Management System) applications, highlighting their interlinking and significance in data collection and system monitoring. Key features of state estimator(SE) are detailed, including real-time sequencing, data filtration, handling various types of measurements, and consistency checks. A comprehensive discussion of the processes involved in achieving an optimal state estimator solution follows, covering SCADA data import, network topology processing, and observability analysis. The paper then delves into specific tuning strategies designed to improve state estimator performance. These strategies include network truncation, verification of network parameters, incorporation of pseudo measurements, correction of ICCP (Inter Control Centre Communication Protocol) mismatches, and network topology corrections, etc. Finally, the paper evaluates the quality of the state estimator solution and the associated objective function values, demonstrating significant improvements through the proposed strategies. This study provides practical and innovative solutions to enhance state estimation in large and complex power networks, contributing to more reliable and efficient power system operations.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Based Overcurrent Relay Supervision Against Cyberattacks: The Role of Data Pre-Processing
abstract: Modern power system substations are digitalized and integrated with different communication technologies. As a result, the power systems became more susceptible to cyber threats. This paper details the application of a deep learning model called convolutional auto-encoder, and the importance of pre-processing the training data to discriminate actual fault from cyberattacked faults in overcurrent relays. The deep learning model is trained utilizing fault data that has undergone data pre-processing. It is discussed how data pre-processing techniques affect the effectiveness of the deep learning model. This study takes into account different cyberattack scenarios, including replay attacks, CT tap setting attacks, and false data injection attacks. The results from testing and validations shows that the suggested strategy can outperform the existing method.

articleTitle: Control of Active Power Oscillations for Unbalance Voltage Mitigation in Inverter-Interfaced Distribution Network
abstract: Increasing levels of distribution energy resources (DERs) and unbalance loads at distribution network often lead to rise in voltage unbalance. The DERs, such as solar based grid connected inverter, can inject negative sequence currents which may cause double frequency power oscillations at the inverter's point of common coupling (PCC). This paper presents a novel decoupled positive-negative sequence controller to improve the voltage unbalance factor (VUF) within the power oscillation limits. In order to ensure smooth inverter operation, the active power oscillation limit is imposed based on active power injection using negative sequence current restrictions. The control of real power oscillation limit, using the negative sequence component, helps to mitigate the unbalanced voltages in the network. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using a radial distribution system integrated with inverter interfaced grid-tied solar inverters in MATLAB. The simulation results for different levels of power injections and unbalanced load conditions shows the influence of real power oscillation limit on mitigating the voltage unbalance in the network.

articleTitle: Challenges and Insights Gained from Upgrading an IEC 61850-Based Substation Automation System - A Comprehensive Case Study
abstract: This paper sheds light on the challenges encountered during the upgrade of mixed-type substations where both conventional and IEC 61850-compliant Substation Automation System (SAS) coexist. The motivation for this upgrade stemmed from the sluggish performance of aging SAS systems, which had become increasingly incompatible with newer 61850-compliant Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs). The introduction of new bays, feeders, and IEDs, coupled with the rapid expansion of the Indian power sector, led to the proliferation of IEDs and the need for SAS upgrades. Recognizing the potential offered by the IEC 61850 standard, POWERGRID embarked on an ambitious SAS system upgrade, aiming to foster interoperability and reduce dependency on single vendors through open competition. This paper presents a case study of the upgrade conducted at a mixed-type substation, featuring over 200 IEC 61850- compliant IEDs from diverse manufacturers. Notably, the upgrade was executed by a vendor specializing in make-x SAS, highlighting the challenges of integrating third-party IEDs into an existing SAS infrastructure. The study explores several integration challenges and lessons learned throughout the project, offering valuable insights for utilities planning similar upgrades. The experiences shared in this paper will aid in smoother transitions and more efficient upgrades for power utilities seeking to maintain the reliability and performance of their critical assets.

articleTitle: Dynamic Line Rating Forecasting Using Bi-LSTM
abstract: Transmission systems worldwide are being upgraded to accommodate massive amounts of renewable energy. The cost of installing new transmission lines is too high, and using static line ratings (SLR) in power system operations only partially utilizes transmission systems. Dynamic line rating (DLR) may improve the power transfer capacity of existing transmission lines, resulting in greater renewable energy utilization and fewer curtailments. DLR depends highly on volatile weather conditions, so it must be forecasted for day-ahead and real-time power system operations. This paper proposes a novel bi-directional long-short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) model-based DLR forecasting methodology considering uncertain weather parameters. The productiveness of the stated procedure is displayed through experimental validation on real-world DLR datasets. A comparison with existing forecasting techniques reflects the superiority of the proposed methodology in terms of predictive accuracy and robustness. The improved DLR forecasts using the proposed model can increase power transmission network resilience and stability.

articleTitle: Enhanced Coordination of FPGA-Based Numerical Relays with Fully Customized Time-Voltage-Current Characteristics for Microgrid Protection
abstract: This paper presents the coordination of numerical relays featuring fully customized time-voltage-current characteristics in microgrids with unified settings essential for both grid-connected and islanded modes of operation. As the coordination framework is a nonlinear constrained optimization problem, a new naturally inspired optimization algorithm, named Ant Lion Optimizer (ALO) is employed to obtain optimal settings. The coordination model is employed on the CIGRE MV benchmark system, which is designed in DIGSILENT. To validate the numerical relay settings, fault data extracted from DIGSILENT is used, and the implementation is carried out on a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) through the MATLAB SIMULINK interface.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Operational Behavior of Standalone Grid-Scale Battery Energy Storage System (BESS): A Chhattisgarh State Case Study
abstract: The effective integration of renewable energy sources (RES) into the power grid is crucial for India's sustainable energy future. This paper presents a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model to optimize the unit commitment (UC) and economic dispatch (ED) of Chhattisgarh's power system, considering the projected demand for FY-26, upcoming generation capacity additions, and the assumed inclusion of two 200 MW/800 MWh BESS plants. The study analyzes the operational behavior of BESS under various scenarios, including high demand and high RE generation weeks. The results highlight the importance of BESS in peak shaving, load leveling, and managing the variability of RES, while also revealing limitations in addressing prolonged energy deficits. The findings contribute valuable insights for policymakers and stakeholders in the Indian power sector, emphasizing the need for strategic BESS integration to ensure grid stability and cost-effectiveness as RES penetration increases.

articleTitle: Exploring Technology and Technical Options to Address Challenges of Transmission Utilities
abstract: This paper highlights real world examples to effectuate smart grid technologies like synchrophasors, and drones. Use of data mining software to adopt smart grid data handling techniques like data compression to address the present-day data communication challenges of the transmission utilities. The paper demonstrates with case studies how synchrophasors assist in exercising better operational management due to enhanced situational awareness of the grid as well as in detecting oscillations present in electrical power system. Drones can be utilized for achieving better operational performance with faster actions to carry patrolling of transmission assets with remedial measures needed. These steps assist in making grid flexible to operate and resilient in response during system degradation.

articleTitle: Oscillation Source Detection for the Indian Power System Using Synchrophasor Measurements
abstract: This paper proposes a data-driven approach to determine the source of forced oscillations occurring due to increased solar generation in the Indian power system. The proposed method utilises the area covered by the trajectory of positive sequence voltage phasor obtained from a phasor data concentrator to detect the oscillation's source. The proposed method is tested for the forced oscillations encountered in the Indian power system on 1st May 2024. Compared to the Dissipating Energy Flow method for oscillation source detection, the results suggest better localisation of forced oscillations, thus giving valuable insights to power system operators for better and more efficient system management.

articleTitle: Input-Output Feedback Linearized Control of Grid-Forming Converters in Virtual Synchronous Machine Mode
abstract: This paper presents a robust input-output feedback linearized voltage control of an inverter operating as a Virtual Synchronous Machine (VSM), enhancing the stability of Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs) in grid systems. IBRs, which replace synchronous generators, pose challenges due to their different dynamic characteristics. The VSM control approach emulates synchronous machine behaviour in IBRs. Input-output feedback linearized control dynamically compensates for the nonlinear dynamics of IBRs, enabling the design of a linear PI regulator and enhancing converter stability. Controller gains are selected using eigenvalue sensitivity analysis. The proposed control is evaluated in a scenario where a synchronous generator is replaced with the IBR in the IEEE 118-bus network, demonstrating the robustness of the proposed control in enhancing grid stability.

articleTitle: Periodic Steady-State Computation for Coupled Field-Circuit Problems
abstract: This paper presents a model-in-the-loop (MIL) approach to solving coupled field-circuit problems using free and open-source software. A field computation software like FEMM is used to obtain a look-up table (LUT) based description of electromagnetic devices. The LUT of flux linkages and electro-magnetic torque are generated for a grid of current values and the positions of the electromagnetic devices. The external lumped circuit is simulated using a numerical integration technique along with the LUT model, using GNU Octave. The transient response of the coupled field circuit is illustrated using two cases: a non-linear inductor connected to a voltage source and a primitive AC generator. The MIL results are validated using the results of Ansys ElectronicsTM. The computation of the periodic steady-state solution of the field-coupled system using an iterative method is also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Control Techniques for MMCs in Unbalanced Grids with Various Transformer Configurations
abstract: The growing application of power electronics devices for integrating renewable energy sources in power systems has become an area of research due to the varied nature of power systems and renewable energies. Imbalances in power systems, resulting from over-voltage and faults, drive the need for performance and stability analysis of modular multilevel converters (MMCs). Depending on the transformer configuration of the MMC, the magnitude of the circulating ground current varies. Therefore, a modification of traditional vector control or an advanced controller is required. This paper implements a sequence controller with a zero sequence controller to suppress the power oscillation and current harmonics depending on transformer configurations. In addition to this, an individual phase controller is also implemented to eliminate the power flow in the faulty lines. Finally, the performance of all presented controllers is compared, and an appropriate controller is suggested according to transformer configuration.

articleTitle: Fault Current Response of Grid-Following Converters Interfaced with Different Transformer Connections
abstract: Converter-interfaced renewable sources regulate the current to their rated value during a fault, unlike synchronous generators. Such sources are generally connected to the grid through filter and transformer. The different winding connections of the transformer have an additional effect on the network voltage and current during fault. This paper presents an analytical information on the presence of positive, negative, and zero sequence components of the current and voltage for various connections of transformer and fault types with converter interfaced sources. The effect of different types of winding such as delta-wye grounded, delta-wye ungrounded, and wye grounded-delta on the voltage and current is enquired. The availability check of different sequence components of voltage and current during different fault types helps in deciding the existing protection schemes for the system. A summary of the performance of overcurrent and voltage based protection in a system with converter interfaced sources accompanying different transformer connections is made.

articleTitle: Conservation Voltage Reduction Integrated EV Control Strategy Toward Self-Sufficiency of Standalone Microgrid
abstract: This research work explores the potential of microgrid technology, specifically focusing on its integration with Conservation Voltage Reduction (CVR) and Electric Vehicles (EVs) to address peak load demands effectively. By integrating CVR and EVs into the microgrid framework, the study aims to create a more resilient and efficient energy system. Notably, the integration of CVR and EVs represents a significant advancement towards the realization of a smart grid infrastructure, where various components interact seamlessly to optimize energy distribution and consumption. Through the development of a robust control algorithm, the research paper demonstrates how the coordinated integration of CVR and EVs can enhance microgrid self-sufficiency while alleviating the load on inverters during periods of high-power demand. Overall, this study contributes to the growing body of research aimed at leveraging innovative technologies to create more sustainable and resilient energy systems. The control scheme is devised using MATLAB, and the outcomes are verified using the same platform.

articleTitle: Synchrophasor Measurement Prediction Using Modified Time-Series Mixer Model Under Cyber Attacks
abstract: Power systems are critical infrastructures that require robust monitoring and control mechanisms to ensure reliability, stability, and efficiency. It utilizes the data from Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) and other monitoring devices, which are sent over communication links. Hence, they are subjected to cyber attacks leading to missing or corrupted values. This can cause unreliable operation of the power system. To address the issue, this paper proposes a modified Time-Series Mixer model to accurately predict multivariate measurements under continuous unavailability of data. The proposed model utilizes the time-mixing and feature-mixing layers, which help to capture temporal and spatial correlation to predict the measurements. Further, it can be utilized in real-time applications in case of attack on any communication channel/PMU measurements, as the single model predicts all the PMU measurements. The performance of the proposed model is validated using data generated for the IEEE 14 bus system via RTDS. Numerical results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, as the errors are significantly smaller than those obtained by the LSTM model-based consecutive PMU measurement prediction technique.

articleTitle: Classification of Power Quality Disturbances Using Convolutional Neural Network and Temporal Convolutional Network Models
abstract: Power quality disturbances (PQDs) have adverse effects on the performance of the electrical equipment and the overall system reliability, and therefore, the detection and diagnosis of PQDs are crucial. Typically, PQDs are classified as batch processing, where a PQD is detected for every 10 fundamental cycles (i.e., 200 ms). Nonetheless, the classification of PQD for every instant gives vital information and can be an online process. This paper presents a deep learning-based model for detecting and classifying 18 PQDs in a noisy environment using 1D Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN). The CNN and TCN facilitate the automatic extraction of meaningful features from the input PQD signals as they evade the typical three-stage classification approach using signal processing techniques. This leads to minimal computational burden and faster classification. Furthermore, the TCN has an additional feature of continuous detection of PQDs at each instant. The performance of the classifiers is measured in terms of classification accuracy and test time. A comparative analysis is performed with a CNN to provide a better insight into the merits of the proposed TCN model. The CNN model outperformed the TCN model by accurately classifying the signal under 20 dB noise. However, the TCN has the advantage of detecting the disturbances at every sample averaged over four samples (i.e., 1.25 ms), whereas the CNN outputs for every 200 ms.

articleTitle: Enhancing State-of-Charge Prediction for PEVs Using Hybrid CNN and LSTM Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: The State of Charge (SoC) estimation of lithiumion batteries is a critical aspect in the domain of plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs), influencing their performance, range, and overall efficiency. This paper addresses the improvements and limitations of SoC estimate methods, with an emphasis on lithium-ion batteries used in PEVs. The paper comprehensively analyzes a range of strategies used to determine SoC, including traditional methods and modern approaches, including model-based predictions and machine-learning (ML) algorithms. This work employs ML techniques such as Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). In order to analyze SoC predictions, this paper proposes a hybrid ML strategy that combines CNN and LSTM. An effective SoC prediction is achieved using CNN, LSTM, and an integration of both. A comparison of the findings shows that the hybrid ML model outperforms CNN and LSTM in predicting the SoC of PEVs. The hybrid model exhibits impressive performance with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.92%, indicating a significant enhancement in accuracy compared to CNN and LSTM, which have MAE values of 2.12% and 4.2%, respectively.

articleTitle: Assessing Load Hosting Capacity: A Demand Response and Economic Approach
abstract: Towards the transition of achieving a highly reliable grid with increased Electric Vehicles (EV) penetration, it is imperative to assess the system's load hosting capacity. As the load increases, so should the adequacy of resources and grid infrastructure. This hosting capacity evaluation is necessary to determine the system's inherent ability to support additional loads before reinforcing new conductors, cables, generating sources, and other grid infrastructure. This evaluation can be done by computing the available power transfer capacity of the active distribution system. On the other hand, load growth can be managed through an appropriate energy management approach that balances the supply and demand of energy. One such strategy is Demand Response (DR), which involves adjusting the electricity consumption of end-users in response to changes in grid conditions and resource availability. EVs have emerged as potential prosumers who can contribute to DR by using their vehicle batteries to store and supply electricity back to the grid as needed. The primary objective of this analysis has two stages: First, to evaluate the system's load hosting capacity by considering simultaneous load growth through an increase in system demand and EV load demand. Second, to incorporate DR in the maximally loaded system by load shifting to ensure that the line's maximum loading capacity is fully utilized with reduced grid import cost. In this analysis, the EVs considered are residential EVs and renewable penetration is also included. This type of hosting capacity analysis, followed by DR, would greatly help end-users and operators to investigate the impacts and take necessary actions for stable and reliable grid operations in the near future. This analysis has been performed for the initial configuration of the IEEE 33 bus system.

articleTitle: Stochastic Resource Adequacy Assessment for DISCOMs with Renewables and Energy Storage
abstract: Resource adequacy assessment is an integral aspect of power system planning and operation, which has become more critical because of the increased penetration of renewable energy resources (RES), demand response, and economy-wide electrification. This paper presents a resource adequacy assessment methodology wherein the representative days are obtained using the k-medoid clustering approach. Further, a novel linear unit commitment formulation (UC) is proposed. The proposed UC formulation performs Monte Carlo simulations to solve large DISCOM problems efficiently. Moreover, value at risk (VaR) and conditional value at risk (CVaR) estimates of loss of load hours and normalized energy not served are evaluated. The estimation of reliability metrics is carried out in line with Central Electricity Authority (CEA) guidelines on resource adequacy framework. Finally, the results for a representative DISCOM, with a peak demand of 25 GW, are presented to demonstrate the approach.

articleTitle: Application of Cybersecurity Policies and Standards in Indian Power Sector
abstract: Cyber security is a critical issue that the distribution system operators, regulators, and industries have recently realized. Attacks on operational technology (OT) can have a severe impact in comparison to information technology (IT). Attack surface in an OT domain increases due to the challenges in patch management, risk assessment, and the knowledge gap among the operators regarding cyber security. IEC 62443 is a standard that aims to fill the specific knowledge gap among OT engineers in cybersecurity. This paper highlights overview of IEC 62351 and proposes mechanisms for the adoption and implementation of IEC 62351 in a uniform, secure, and interoperable manner. This paper discusses the applicability of IEC 62351 for substation and control center communication and touches upon the importance of IEC 62443 for secure development lifecycle requirements in industrial automation and control systems.

articleTitle: A Pragmatic Approach to Integrated Hybrid State Estimation in Rectangular Coordinates
abstract: Traditional transmission and distribution state estimators have been based on SCADA system. Deployment of PMUs in grid calls for a hybrid state estimator (HSE). This proposition is tricky because of different time scales of updates of the two technologies as well as order of difference in time skew errors. We propose a pragmatic approach to HSE. We bring out that rectangular coordinates would be more appropriate and propose an adaptive weights allocation strategy for RTU measurement to address technology adaption challenges. Simulation results on IEEE-14 and IEEE-118 bus systems demonstrates the claims made. The paper also serves as a concise tutorial for HSE development.

articleTitle: A Maximum Mean Discrepancy Estimator Enabled Cyber Attack Detection in an Autonomous AC Microgrid
abstract: This paper presents a novel scheme to precisely identify cyber attacks, such as controller hijacking and unauthorized data modification, which can compromise an autonomous microgrid's (MG) frequency and voltage stability. The scheme is based on the Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) index, which calculates the unbiased estimates of local voltage/frequency synchronizing tracking errors for each Distributed Energy Resource (DER). Under the compromised situation, MMD accurately and quickly distinguishes the attacked DER from the uncompromised DERs. The efficacy of the proposed cyber-attack detection scheme is tested under various types of cyber attacks on the IEEE-13 bus distribution feeder, modelled in RSCAD and is validated with Real Time Digital Simulator (RTDS) platform integrated with dSPACE 1104 R&D automation controller through Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) simulation control environment.

articleTitle: Framework for Post-Facto Analysis of Wide-area Power System Disturbances and Events
abstract: After a major wide-area power system disturbance, a multitude of disturbance data is generated in the form of disturbance records, phasor data, sequence of events, etc. These collated datasets are processed by power system consultants or system operators to perform post-mortem analysis. The preliminary steps are filtering and labeling the data, obtaining derived quantities, aligning the asynchronous data, and segmenting the disturbance data to detect features that support the analysis. This paper presents the signal processing aspects of performing a generic post-mortem analysis. A user interface (UI) with semi-automatic stages is prepared around these developments. Though the UI tool was developed using Qt Designer and the versatile Python language for back-end scripting, the process is software-agnostic. Practical data from the 2020 Mumbai blackout is used for the illustration.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning-Assisted Volt/VAR Management in Unbalanced Distribution Network with Prosumer DER and EV Charging Loads
abstract: Large-scale deployment of cutting-edge technologies such as distributed generation, electric vehicle charging stations, and prosumer distributed energy resources (DER) have drawn the attention of system operators and grid planners towards energy management and smooth operation of distribution grids. In this context, an artificial intelligence-assisted hierarchically controlled energy management framework for the unbalanced distribution grid operation and control has been introduced. The two-level approach has been adopted in this study. The first level is known for centralized management and the second for local management of energy and network operations. The proposed centralized model predictive control (MPC) based volt/VAR management (VVM) model for voltage/VAR optimization has been successfully implemented along with EV charging loads and prosumer DERs. The fruitful utilization of artificial neural networks has been done while developing reinforcement learning (RL) based local controller to manage the voltage locally. The impact of the proposed RL-based local control has been compared with the traditional droop-based voltage control method which is based on local measurement with minimum communication requirement. The proposed hierarchical energy management framework has been validated through a modified IEEE 34 bus feeder unbalanced distribution test system. The simulated model of OpenDSS interfaced with Python for the considered test illustrates that the proposed hierarchical control framework is capable of managing the energy demand of the distribution system and controlling the voltage profile under uncertain scenarios and transient events.

articleTitle: Detection of HRF in Battery Energy Storage System
abstract: Integrating renewable energy sources into the grid has raised stability concerns, necessitating a grid-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) deployment to enhance transient stability. However, incorporating various control techniques in such a system to meet the voltage, power requirements, and grid code compliance can challenge conventional relaying schemes due to current and voltage modulation during a fault. Further, high resistance faults may cause minimal changes in relay current and voltage during the fault, causing non-detection of the fault. As a result, the BESS will feed its energy to the fault, which is unacceptable. This paper presents a protection scheme capable of fault detection in microgrids. The method employs the Hilbert Transform to relay current, and following that, mathematical morphology is applied to decompose the signal further to detect small changes during any disturbance. The various simulation results on a 25 kW / 700 V DC battery storage system simulated in MATLAB/SIMULINK reveal that the proposed method is highly accurate in detecting high resistance faults.

articleTitle: Optimal Site Selection of the PV Plant in North-Eastern Region of India Using AHP-BWM Techniques
abstract: Development of renewable energy sources like photovoltaic systems is imperative as our reliance on fossil fuels is a threat to the climate and the energy supply for future generations. However, inappropriate PV site selection could lead to compromised output. Therefore, an effective technique is required for finding out the most significant factors in selecting the location of solar PV plants. In this paper, a multi-criteria decision making (MCDM) technique is proposed for selecting an optimal location for installing a solar PV plant in the North-East region of India. A PV plant's optimal location must balance qualitative and quantitative factors, including irradiance, sunlight hours, grid distance, and existing installations. In this paper, the best criteria for site selection and the most suitable state for a PV plant set up are determined by applying the Best-Worst Method (BWM) and Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). The comparative study of both methods and the sensitivity analysis has been carried out to find out the most significant parameters. A sensitivity analysis has been conducted to assess the impact of change in input parameters on the optimal location of solar PV plant. The simulation results shows that the state of Assam, India is the best place for the solar power plants installation, whereas the state of Meghalaya is the least suited place.

articleTitle: Enhancing Efficiency, Effectiveness and Resiliency of Indian Load Dispatch Centers Through Institutional Capacity Building: Analysis, Impacts and Way Forward
abstract: Load Despatch Centres (LDCs) in India ensure the reliable, secure, and efficient operation of one of the largest synchronous grids in the world. This paper highlights the institutional capacity-building initiatives taken by the Ministry of Power, Govt. of India, FOLD and Grid-India. The paper also presents the analysis of the benchmarking survey done for the 3rd LDC Excellence Awards in 2023. All forty-two LDCs participated in the survey. This benchmarking exercise promotes collaboration, enabling LDCs to share best practices and find areas for improvement, ensuring readiness for future challenges. The primary goal of these initiatives is to establish institutional arrangements for continuous excellence in the functioning of LDCs. This paper highlights the recent initiatives, the impact of these initiatives, and the way forward.

articleTitle: Investigation of Low Frequency Power System Oscillations in North Eastern Regional Grid of India
abstract: The widespread adoption of phasor measurement units throughout the Indian power grid enables the observation and analysis of comprehensive system dynamics. Among these dynamics, low-frequency oscillation stands out as a significant phenomenon. The study examines recent LFO incidents on September 10, 2023, at 14:53 and May 28, 2023, at 00:36, using the matrix pencil method for accurate identification of oscillation modes amidst noise, essential for real-time monitoring with PMUs. Case analyses reveal specific events of September 10, 2023, a significant oscillation event was triggered by a fault in the Doyang generating unit's evacuation line, while on May 28, 2023, oscillations resulted from a generation loss outside North-Eastern Region impacting the Silchar PMU bus. The study underscores the imperative of precise PSS tuning aligned with identified oscillatory modes to sustain grid stability in NER, advocating for adjustments in controller time constants and stabilizer gains based on thorough modal analysis using matrix pencil method. It was found that neglecting comprehensive PSS tuning, particularly for governor outputs and only considering exciter outputs, poses risks to system stability, as demonstrated by persistent oscillations observed in both analyzed events. The study prioritize governor step response and exciter tests to optimize PSS performance across operational scenarios, ensuring robust stability measures for the NER grid.

articleTitle: Planning and Operational Analysis of India's Power System for Green Hydrogen Production
abstract: Achieving India's 5 million tonnes (MT) green hydrogen (GH2) production target by 2030 will be marred by serious challenges as this will require the large-scale integration of renewable energy (RE) into the grid, which, due to its intermittent nature is bound to impact grid operations significantly. This study aims to assess the implication of GH2 production on grid operations with a power system simulation exercise by determining the optimal RE and electrolyser capacities. The simulation output shows that 135 GW of RE capacity with 84 GW wind and 51 GW solar is required to generate 310 billion units of electricity to power 74 GW of electrolyser capacity with a peak demand of 409 GW, an increase of 67 GW (compared to BAU demand in 2030 without GH2 load). The battery storage requirement is reduced by 6 GW to 38 GW due to the utilization of surplus RE power to meet the GH2 electricity demand. An investment requirement of around INR 10.6 lakh crores is estimated to meet the GH2 target. Producing GH2 without Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) support increases RE requirement by 10 GW to 145 GW and the cost of hydrogen generation by 14 percent to USD 4.1/kg. The study recommends undertaking rigorous transmission planning exercise, recognising electrolyser as flexibility source, developing grid connectivity standards for electrolysers, and forming an industry consortium to promote large-scale grid-connected GH2 pilots.

articleTitle: Optimised Calibration of Travelling Wave Based Fault Locator System for Accurately Locating Transmission Line Faults
abstract: Transmission lines are essential for power distribution over long distances, but they are prone to faults due to various factors. Impedance-based fault locators have been widely adopted, but their precision remains a challenge. Travelling Wave-based Fault Locators offer promise in this regard, leveraging wave propagation characteristics for accurate fault localization. This paper comprehensively examines fault scenarios, impedance-based methods, and the principles of Traveling Wave based Fault Locator (TWFL). It also discusses optimized architecture and configuration designs for Traveling Wave Fault Locators (TWFL), addressing challenges and presenting field case analyses. The significance of calibrated TWFL systems in enhancing fault location accuracy and ensuring grid reliability is underscored, offering valuable insights for practitioners and researchers in transmission line maintenance and fault detection.

articleTitle: Optimal Network Clustering in Edge Computing Architecture for Distribution Network Monitoring
abstract: The management of large measurement sets within power systems for state estimation (SE) imposes a communication burden, consequently leading to delays in SE. To address the above challenges, this paper proposes an optimal edge-computing architecture to provide robust support for SE. Potential edge estimation points (EEPs) are identified, which function as edge servers (ESs), responsible for estimating nodes within clusters. An initial network clustering scheme is established using a novel network evolution concept and electrical distance analysis. To achieve the optimal allocation of EEPs and clustering in alignment with the defined objectives, a modified mutation operator is introduced within a genetic algorithm (GA), tailored to the network's topology. The objectives are designed to streamline the SE process and generate appropriate clusters. A comprehensive analysis of the IEEE 123-bus system has been conducted, revealing a multitude of viable EEP-laden clusters suitable for SE, thereby showcasing the effectiveness of the optimization approach. The solutions outperform the benchmark solutions. Furthermore, the algorithm showcases fast convergence, underscoring its efficiency in addressing the evolving demands of distribution network management.

articleTitle: Voltage Control of Active Distribution Networks with Photovoltaic Systems and Residential Electric Vehicle Charger Penetration Using Model Predictive Control
abstract: The increasing photovoltaic (PV) penetration and electric vehicle (EV) loads lead to frequent and uncertain voltage fluctuations in active distribution networks (ADNs). This paper presents a multi-time scale real-time hybrid coordinated control strategy, based on the model predictive control, for voltage regulation and loss minimization in ADNs. The proposed control scheme regulates voltages in the presence of PVs and residential EV charging, leveraging real-world data sets. The centralized control mechanism coordinates the on-load tap changer, PV systems, and EV charging stations through multi-time step optimization models, using receding horizon control. Additionally, a rapid-response local control mechanism, operating on a timescale of a few seconds, is employed to mitigate frequent voltage violations and serve as a contingency measure in the event of a failure in the centralized control scheme. The developed control scheme is validated on the 33-bus distribution network and the IEEE 123-bus distribution network. The maximum/ minimum voltages in 33-bus network are seen to be 1.046/ 0.950 p.u. as compared to 1.063/ 0.87 p.u. in uncontrolled case, with 31.7% reduction in energy losses.

articleTitle: Enhancing Grid Stability and Economic Efficiency Through Geographically Diversified Solar PV Deployment: A Case Study of the North-Eastern Region of India
abstract: India increasingly relies on solar photovoltaics (PV) to harness its vast solar energy potential and combat climate change. However, the current PV capacity is predominantly concentrated in nine states, excluding regions like the North-Eastern Region (NER) of India. This study investigates the impact of diversifying solar power generation on the national grid, focusing on the NER. Methodologically, the research aims to verify whether distributing PV sites across different regions can alleviate the risks of low PV generation and high variability. Additionally, it seeks to verify several benefits of geographically dispersed PV generation, including extended PV generation periods.increased capacity for PV installation, enhanced diversity factor, reduced storage and ramping requirements, and better utilization of the North-Eastern grid of India's hydroelectric potential. Results indicate that the NER experiences early morning solar peak hours, which closely align with the peak demand hours across India. This synchronism presents an opportunity to mitigate peak hour demands nationwide without relying on gas-fired plants or expensive battery storage solutions. This strategy not only supports grid decarbonization but also offers a cost-effective approach. Moreover, diversifying PV plants across India, particularly in the NER, enhances the diversity factor of solar generation and optimizes the utilization of the region's abundant hydroelectric potential. This research underscores the advantages of geographically dispersed PV installations in mitigating PV generation variability due to weather patterns, enhancing grid stability, and leveraging regional strengths such as hydroelectric power in the NER. By strategically locating PV installations, India can strengthen its renewable energy infrastructure while promoting economic efficiency and sustainability.

articleTitle: Enhancing Auto Recloser Insights with PMU Data
abstract: Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) data have revolutionized system operations significantly with improvement in the decision-making process during power restoration by reducing dependency on traditional field communications, which often led to delays. Even with a limited number of PMUs, real-time event detection has become possible. The paper presents a data-driven analytical methodology which serves as a First Information Report (FIR) by generating a report within one minute of the occurrence of fault. This is in-house developed analytics at SLDC of Telangana State, which provides fault signature analysis for the system operator. Additionally, the FIR supplements the sequence of events(SoE) and disturbance recorder(DR) reports which are prepared later. Four real-time case studies are prepared to focus on Auto-Recloser(AR) operations during single line-to-ground (SLG) faults. The primary objective is to demonstrate the effectiveness of the data driven analytics in both near real-time and offline reporting, offering timely insights well ahead of traditional DR and SoE systems.

articleTitle: An Iterative Method to Effectively Filter-Out Harmonics Injected by High-Speed Railways
abstract: High-speed railway (HSR) operations are increasingly recognized for their sustainability in electric transportation. However, the nonlinear characteristics of traction loads introduce harmonic currents into power systems. These harmonics generated during HSR operations have a critical frequency range of 1.5-2 kHz, which significantly impact the grid by increasing system losses and degrading equipment performance. Addressing this issue requires effectively filtering out these harmonics at the interface of traction systems to prevent distortions from entering the power supply. Existing filter designs for traction often overlook higher-order frequencies, and there is limited focus on the optimal placement and use of filters for reactive power compensation. This paper proposes an effective harmonics filtering technique to regulate the impact of harmonics generated by onboard HSRs within permissible limits. Additionally, a heuristic algorithm is developed to determine the optimal placement of these filters along the feeding section and analyze the reactive power compensation provided by the filters. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated on a real HSR track in India. The results validated against the IEEE-519 standard for harmonic control in electrical power systems, show significant improvements in total harmonic distortions of current and voltage compared to instances without filters.

articleTitle: Enhanced Fault Current Utilization by Grid-Forming Inverter Using Non-Linear Transient Virtual Resistance During Symmetrical Faults
abstract: The next-generation grid-forming inverters are more prone to overcurrent issues during grid faults due to their voltage source behaviour behind the impedance. This issue can be over-come by using the virtual resistance (VR) drop feedback and reconstructing the voltage reference for the inverter. Existing literature prefers transient VR (TVR) over VR to avoid the risk of transient instability. This paper proposes a novel nonlinear transient virtual resistance (NLTVR) method to restrict the fault current for the droop-controlled grid-forming three-phase inverter modelled in the stationary reference frame. The parameter design of the proposed NLTVR method is analyzed and the optimum selection is evaluated in a wide range of grid strengths as well as fault severity. Additionally, the low voltage ride-through (LVRT) performance of the inverter, along with the proposed method in the case of a symmetrical fault, is simulated and compared using MATLAB/Simulink. The results demonstrate that the proposed method improves the maximum fault current utilization capability of the inverter in comparison to state-of-the-art linear and nonlinear TVR methods during faults.

articleTitle: Effect of Simultaneous FDI and DoS Attack of Multi-Area Power System with Dynamic Event-Triggering Algorithm
abstract: The twenty-first century comes with advancements in information technology, which positively upgrades the conventional communication infrastructure. However, this improvement comes at the price of compromised system security. Broadly, the attackers can hamper normalcy in any system in two ways: firstly, falsifying data through the network in a false data injection (FDI) type attack; secondly, the attackers will make the network unavailable for communication in denial of service (DoS) attack. Lately, in a real-world scenario, the attackers are incorporating hybrid attacks, i.e., combining the above-mentioned attacks to damage the system performance further. The automatic load frequency control (ALFC) incorporated in modern smart grids relies on communication channels, so any interference in data can result in frequency diversion and instability in the system. Thus, a resilient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf> controller, which is verified to be exponentially stable, designed by Lyapunov Krasovskii functional (LKF), is implemented in this work. The dynamic event-triggering algorithm (DETA) scheme is also incorporated with the controller to save on bandwidth use. The linear matrix inequality (LMI) method is used to find the controller's gain and weight of the event-triggered system of the three-area power system to verify the effectiveness of the designed controller.

articleTitle: Review on Residential Rooftop Solar Status in India
abstract: This paper explores the potential for rooftop solar installations in India, elucidates the current state of these installations, and outlines various governmental initiatives aimed at augmenting rooftop solar infrastructure. It examines the impact of conventional schemes such as net metering and feed-in tariffs within the Indian context, as well as the emergence of virtual net metering and peer-to-peer (P2P) energy sharing models in fostering the expansion of rooftop solar (RTS) systems. Additionally, it analyzes the advantages and drawbacks associated with distinct business models, including capital expenditure (CAPEX) and renewable energy service company (RESCO) models. Finally, it discusses short-term and long-term recommendations for the growth of rooftop solar in India.

articleTitle: Optimal Location and Sizing of Fast Charging Stations for Electric Vehicles in Guwahati City Using Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II
abstract: Finding an optimal location and sizing of fast charging stations for electric vehicles (EVs) has plagued the research community for over a decade. The adoption of EVs in the transportation sector has been affected by the range anxiety and availability of fast chargers. Researchers have attempted to tackle the location and sizing problems using various methods. Of these, evolutionary algorithms have offered prominent meaningful solutions. Electric vehicle fast charging point operators and users of EVs are two important cogs in the wheel. The operator of an EV fast charging station needs to maximize profit to maintain operability, while the EV users look at charging comfort as the most important factor. Generally, both of these objectives are conflicting in nature, and thus, it requires a nondominated sorting multi-objective optimization algorithm to solve this problem. This paper addresses this problem for the Indian city of Guwahati to offer an optimized solution for the location and sizing of fast charging stations for EVs for the expected demand by the year 2030. A fast and elitist multiobjective non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm-II (NSGA-II) has been used to solve a bi-objective optimization problem. Postpareto analysis has been carried out to identify the most effective pareto-optimal solution. Simulations have been performed in MATLAB/SIMULINK to obtain the optimal location and sizing of fast charging stations for EVs in Guwahati city.

articleTitle: Large-Signal Stability Analysis of Renewable-Based Islanded AC Microgrids with Static and Dynamic Loads: An Overview
abstract: Microgrids (MGs) are essential for the smooth integration of distributed energy resources (DERs), including renewable energy sources (RESs) and distributed energy storage systems (DESSs), into the modern electric grid. This integration helps to ensure a reliable and resilient power supply to the critical loads, especially, during islanded mode of operation of AC microgrids (ACMGs). However, the nonlinear behavior of the power electronics interfaced DERs and low or no inertia contribution by these can cause serious stability problems in RESs-based islanded ACMGs with static and dynamic loads.
