Stability analysis of islanded ACMGs can be performed for small-signal and large-signal disturbances using small-signal and large-signal stability analysis methods, respectively. Small-signal stability analysis of islanded ACMGs, with static and dynamic loads, has been studied numerously and several findings have been reported in the existing literature. However, the large-signal stability analysis of islanded ACMGs, with static and dynamic loads, remains a major difficulty and it has received limited research attention. Therefore, this paper provides an overview of the recent developments, technical issues, and emerging trends in the large-signal stability analysis of renewable-based islanded ACMGs with static and dynamic loads.

articleTitle: Bad Data Detection and Elimination of Faulty Meter Measurements of Power Grid
abstract: The review and evaluation of bad data detection and elimination methods in power system state estimation highlights the evolution from traditional techniques to modern, data-driven approaches. This research paper discusses various approaches to handling bad data, such as chi-square testing, residual-based methods, and Gaussian-based methods. These methods are either inaccurate, computationally inefficient, or complex. The Largest Normalized Residual (LNR) test, a widely used method for identifying faulty data in power system state estimation (PSSE), has proven effective for single and non-interacting multiple erroneous data. However, the LNR test becomes computationally inefficient in large-scale systems with significant bad data due to its sequential removal process. In this paper we have implemented a modified LNR test method. The idea behind the algorithm is to classify the suspect measurements into groups and simultaneously apply the LNR test to each group, thereby detecting multiple instances of bad data across different groups. MATLAB software have been used to implement algorithm for state estimation and bad data techniques on IEEE standard system and Indian real time system. SRLDC or other RLDCs involves large number of meters to measure energy flow at each interface points. Discrepancies in meter recordings (due to faults) and data validations involves manual intervention, leading to significant losses. The goal of this work is to provide an automated, robust state estimation and bad data technique specifically designed for Indian systems, beneficial for both research and industrial applications.

articleTitle: Merging and Splitting of Power System Control Areas - Experience in Western Regional Grid of India
abstract: The Indian Electricity Grid Code 2023 defines the term ‘control area’ as an electrical system bounded by interconnections (tie lines), metering and telemetry, which controls its generation and/or load to maintain its interchange schedule with other control areas and contributes to the regulation of frequency. This paper discusses the experience of Western Regional Load Despatch Centre in merging power system control areas of UT of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and UT of Daman and Diu and splitting of power system control area of BALCO Limited into two separate entities viz. BALCO Generator and BALCO Bulk Consumer. The size of both the control areas, subjected to merger or splitting are bigger than 1 Gigawatt capacity. Such merger and demerger of control areas is unique in nature and require institutional reorganization as well as meticulous planning and coordination to ensure a smooth transition. The paper highlights key challenges faced during the implementation and changes in the scheduling, metering, accounting philosophy during the control area merger and splitting.

articleTitle: An Accurate Single-Ended Fault Locator for Renewables-Integrated Transmission Grid
abstract: Single ended fault location is a desirable feature for utility customers in any local measurement-based protection Intelligent Electronic Device (IED). Like many other power system applications, the modulated voltage and current output of converter interfaced renewable energy sources have posed challenges to existing single-ended fault location methods also. Increased system non-homogeneity introduced by these sources introduces large error in the calculated fault location, which is further aggravated for faults with higher fault resistance. This paper presents an accurate single-ended fault locator for lines connected to such sources. The method involves evaluation of the expression for corrected impedance seen from the local terminal at the two fault location boundary conditions. The final fault location is calculated from the final corrected impedance which is a weighted average of the two boundary evaluations. The method is proved to be robust against various factors including fault location, fault resistance, fault type, and the type of source. Comparison with existing commercially employed method and validation with four geographically scattered field events demonstrate the accuracy and practical applicability of the method.

articleTitle: Battery Energy Storage Based Wide Area Damping Controller to Mitigate Small Signal Oscillations
abstract: Small signal oscillations are a challenge to the stability of power systems, especially with increasing distributed energy resources (DERs). With the increased deployments of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), supplementary damping control mechanisms can be developed to dampen the inter-area oscillations effectively. A wide area damping controller (WADC) for BESS is presented in this work. The first step is to design a Kalman filter to estimate the dynamic states of the system from the synchrophasor measurements. In the next step, using the estimated states, a novel two-step optimization approach is used to develop a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> state feedback controller. The wide area controller output is given as additional input to the control scheme of BESS. This work also considers practical issues in a typical wide-area damping control scheme, such as communication time delays. The developed controller's effectiveness has been verified by simulations on the IEEE 39 bus system and Southern Power Grid System in India. The control scheme that is proposed has also been executed on a real-time testbed using a Real Time Digital Simulator (RTDS), hardware Phasor Measurement Units, and Phasor Data Concentrator (PDC).

articleTitle: A New Approach to Modeling Switching in Power Electronics Networks
abstract: A novel approach to modeling switches in power electronics networks is proposed. Modified solutions are obtained with compensation techniques based on inverse matrix modification. The method results in a discrete-time switch model with a constant conductance in parallel with a controlled current source. The system admittance matrix remains constant regardless of the states of the switches in the circuit. The required solution is obtained more economically by appropriately compensating the network solution using matrix modification methods. This is an elegant approach devoid of any approximation or convergence limitations. The paper shows that the compensation-based technique can be effectively applied to power electronics network models in electromagnetic transient simulation programs. The proposed model of the switch is validated by comparing solutions obtained with commercial-grade transient simulation programs. Examples emphasizing the effectiveness of the compensation-based approach for power electronics simulation are presented.

articleTitle: Considerations for Introducing Distribution System Operators in India
abstract: With the advent of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs), the power distribution sector is witnessing immense challenges in both operational and financial aspects. Hence, countries across the globe are embracing the Distribution System Operator (DSO) concept to address these challenges in the backdrop of ambitious net-zero targets. A DSO-like entity is envisaged to gather, process, and facilitate distribution level granular data and execute the control actions for maintaining reliable and economical distribution system operation. This paper has attempted to highlight various DSO functions and their mapping with existing codes and regulations. Different legal and regulatory considerations and four institutional frameworks are discussed for introducing DSOs in India. Three options are evaluated for distribution system operations: System Operations under the Distribution Licensee, System Operations under Sub-SLDC, and System Operations through Statutory Provision. Due to the diversity of distribution models and varying local needs, States will have different motivations for selecting specific DSO options. Since building institutions is a time-consuming process, it is recommended that the implementation of the DSO be approached incrementally and in phases.

articleTitle: Phase-Specific Active and Reactive Power Injection in Unbalanced Distribution Network with Different Load Models
abstract: Maintaining an adequate voltage balance in distribution networks has become more challenging due to the growing use of uncertain distributed generation (DGs) resources and the asymmetrical distribution of dynamic loads. With the advent of electronic control strategies, smart-inverter-assisted DGs have gained the capability of phase-independent power injection. This feature presents an emerging opportunity to employ DGs to tackle voltage imbalances. This paper introduces an optimization framework to determine the phase-specific active and reactive power schedule in low-voltage distribution networks. Furthermore, this research analyzes the potential of the proposed power injection approach to improve network performance in scenarios where different kinds of loads predominate. The proposed approach has been implemented on IEEE European's unbalanced distribution network. The comparative assessment of the proposed approach with other power injection scenarios demonstrates that the proposed phase-specific power injection approach retains the advantages of balanced power scheduling while also addressing voltage imbalance. The proposed approach is useful for system operators intending to enhance network performance amid steady-state voltage imbalance.

articleTitle: Towards Physics-aware Neural Networks for Distribution Systems State & Parameter Estimation
abstract: Scarcity of real-time measurements and uncertain (or rather outdated) network information hinder the task of state estimation in electrical distribution networks. In this paper, we address this challenge by introducing a neural network-based approach, which jointly estimates the state and the line parameters of a single phased radial power distribution network. Since, in these networks, the line parameters vary gradually, they are assumed to be fixed but unknown over the time-period of interest, while the steady-state voltage evolves based on the re-cently introduced lossy distribution flow equations. The proposed approach considers the measured bus power injection data and the voltage pseudo-measurements of the network and performs the estimation task into three-stages: learns the drift matrix and bus voltages employing the inverse Physics-Informed Neural Network (iPINN) paradigm, estimates the network impedance from the learnt drift matrix through a least-square optimization, and predicts line current and power flows algebraically. We implement the proposed approach on the modified IEEE 33-bus distribution network and find it provides more accurate voltage and impedance estimates considering other machine learning techniques, which require exact network information.

articleTitle: Benefits of Integrating Indian Electricity Market Segments and Regulated Dispatch Stacks
abstract: This paper discusses the potential benefits of coupling Power Exchanges (PX) with the scheduling of interstate generators (ISGS) undertaken by Grid-India through its Security Constrained Economic Dispatch (SCED) mechanism, in the Indian Power System. The fundamental premise for the analysis presented here is to show that there is potentially significant arbitrage opportunity among interstate generators with regulated tariff and their counterparts participating in the PXs that can be elicited by adding a layer of market coupling. This coupling across the incumbent Real-Time Market (RTM) and interstate SCED should be implementable through a Market Coupling Operator (MCO) with relative ease. It may also be extended to the day-ahead market (DAM) in due course of time when the Day Ahead SCED/SCUC (Security Constrained Unit Commitment) is operationalized. Our analysis covered SCED with the Indian Energy Exchange (IEX) that accounts for more than 90% of the PX volume. The analysis first considered a “full-stack” optimization covering the entire ISGS capacity for August 1, 2022, to July 31,2023 without considering the schedule to individual states. It shows that the total annual benefits of coupling could be just over Rs 1000 crores on RTM alone, i.e., daily benefits around Rs 3 crores/day. This was followed by a pre-pilot scale analysis on a day-by-day basis assuming the actual allocation and coarse PX data for October-December 2023, which showed a reduced but still significant savings of 0.7 crore/day. Both analyses also revealed other non-monetary benefits including a reduction in price volatility in IEX including a significant reduction in high price (at or close to price cap) events, massive reduction in number of instructions to ISGS plants to change their schedule that would otherwise be needed, and also avoided ramping shortfall.

articleTitle: Power Market Monitoring in India and Way Forward
abstract: Pre-independence era, the Electricity Act 1910 was the first significant legislative step in regulating electricity generation, transmission, and distribution. The Electricity Act 2003 introduced provisions for delicensing generation, open access, competition, market, and regulatory oversight. The National Electricity Policy formulated in 2005, outlined objectives for electricity sector development, including promoting competition, encouraging private investment, and ensuring quality and reliability of supply. The Government of India has taken major steps to administer electricity market and promote green energy market at National level window through National Open Access Registry (NOAR) and Green Open Access Registry (GOAR) [1], [2]. This has facilitated a common electronic platform accessible to all stakeholders including all authorities to administer the short-term electricity market right from registration of entity till accounting, scheduling of power, payment and reconciliation. This National level platform National Open Access Registry (NOAR) and Green Open Access Registry (GOAR) have also facilitated integration of renewable energy into the country's national grid. The electricity market in India is undergoing significant transformations driven by the integration of renewable energy sources, evolving regulatory frameworks, and increasing demand. Effective monitoring of this dynamic market is crucial for ensuring reliability, efficiency, and competitiveness. The independent role of market monitor enables the effective and transparent operation of the market segments. Further, the electricity being generated flows as per the lows of physics and it cannot be stored for longer duration like other commodities. Thus, the electricity market is different than other commodity market where effective market monitoring plays important role. This paper presents the electricity market monitoring and analysis in India, practices followed across the globe.

articleTitle: Transformer-Based Short-Term Residential Load Forecasting Integrated Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading
abstract: Short-term load forecasting (STLF) is crucial in energy management, offering essential insights for effective operational planning and decision-making, facilitating efficient energy trading. This manuscript aims to integrate STLF with peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading within a residential community microgrid. This methodology employs the mid-market rate (MMR) based pricing mechanism for P2P energy trading in conjunction with STLF techniques. Various deep-learning models known for capturing intricate patterns are used for accurate STLF. After comparative analysis, the transformer model with multi-head attention emerges as the most effective method to achieve a reduced mean squared error and mean absolute error. Subsequently, the optimized STLF model is applied to a community-based P2P energy market, with energy trading prices determined using the MMR method. Overall energy costs decreased significantly compared to the traditional peer-to-grid method. This integrated approach not only optimizes energy trading decisions but also enhances the reliable and efficient use of distributed energy resources.

articleTitle: Development of Data Visualisation Dashboard and Benchmarking of NEA's Load Dispatch Centre's Data Acquisition System and its Integration with South Asia Energy Database
abstract: This paper elaborates the success story behind development of the visualization dashboard and benchmarking of the data acquisition system, located at Nepal Electricity Authority's (NEA's) Load Dispatch Centre (LDC), Kathmandu and presently used for operating the electricity grid of Nepal. Under the project, activities have been carried out towards augmenting the LDC's Real Time Data Acquisition System (RTDAS), Management Information System (MIS) and Data Dissemination by developing an offline database, comprising of the data from existing SCADA system as well as integrating it with offline data captured through manual efforts. The activities also include carrying out gap analysis and suggesting ways towards enhancing the NEA's Load Dispatch Centre's IT infrastructure and data management eco-system. The realization of this regional project has been the outcome of a successful and joint initiative between Nepal Electricity Authority's Load Dispatch Centre (LDC), Kathmandu, Nepal and USAID's South Asia Regional Energy Partnership (SAREP) Program, New Delhi India. The project will immensely help and support NEA in operating the electricity grid of Nepal with enhanced level of safety and security as well as for carrying out the Cross Border Electricity Trade (CBET) in a most economic and efficient manner along with development of the LDC's Strengthening Action Plan for the state-of-the-art RTDAS, MIS and data dissemination.

articleTitle: Dynamic Security Assessment in Renewable-Integrated Power Systems: A Dynamic State Estimation Approach
abstract: This paper presents a model-driven method for the dynamic security assessment based on dynamic state estimation. The dynamic state estimation employs the sub-transient model of the synchronous generator and an unscented Kalman filter for estimating the system states. The pressing need to evaluate security margins in power systems amidst the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources is addressed in the paper. The presented method not only overcomes some of the challenges associated with widely prevailing data-driven methods in literature but also offers enhanced accuracy and adaptability under both steady-state and dynamic conditions. The efficacy of the presented method is validated through several case studies using Kundur's two-area system, including the integration of a renewable energy source. The results from case studies demonstrate that the presented method has a maximum root mean square error of 1.8% under steady-state conditions and 2.5% under dynamic conditions with a renewable energy source. The method is envisioned to have potential applications in power system control centers by proactively averting system collapse through timely control actions.

articleTitle: Unique Transformer Neural Network Based Line Fault Detection Technique in DC Microgrid
abstract: The complexity of DC microgrid protection arises from the need for rapid fault detection, compounded by data limitations and small system restoration windows. This paper explores the use of Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Long-Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Transformer NN (TNN) models for line fault detection in DC microgrids. A novel method based on the modified TNN model is proposed, leveraging measurements from both ends of the DC microgrid line. A total of 1060 unique Pole-to-Ground, Pole-to-Pole, and no-fault scenarios are simulated using the Real-Time Digital Simulator (RTDS), and a few initial samples of line current, bus voltage and associated derived variables are used for training. The proposed method overcomes the DC microgrid constraints, such as the availability of a few parameters and quick detection requirements, by detecting line faults within 10 samples, i.e., 0.6ms, as compared to RNN and LSTM. The method's high accuracy is attributed to increased feature use, such as end currents, bus voltages, and associated current and voltage sample-wise differences. The proposed method can also appropriately identify an event with few missing current samples by utilizing the voltage variations.

articleTitle: Novel Techniques of High Voltage Detection and its Application for Enhancing Safety in Extra High Voltage System Operation and Maintenance
abstract: The safety of maintenance personnel in an Extra High Voltage (EHV) system relies heavily on accurately determining the state of network elements. False judgment during maintenance activities can result in close contact with charged elements, leading to potential injury. Maloperations during maintenance not only pose risks to personal safety but also perturb the overall grid. Current methods for assessing the state of EHV networks primarily rely on data from grid-level Current and Voltage Transformers. A novel technique for Extra High Voltage detection has been developed, based on leakage current in the air. The developed technique involves using a portable device with a field probe, operated within a specified safe distance from charged network elements. Leakage current measurements obtained by the portable device are utilized to display the state of the EHV network element to maintenance personnel in real-time. The EHV field pattern generated by charged network elements can be identified through the measured leakage current. Data collected over an extended period can be employed to assess the health of network elements and conductors. The proposed technique enhances safety, prevents false judgments, and contributes to the overall stability of the EHV grid.

articleTitle: Detailed Phasor Modelling of Grid Forming Proton Exchange Membrane (PEM) Electrolyzer Load
abstract: Hydrogen electrolyzers can serve as grid-forming load, help integrating variable renewable energy sources into the power grids by providing essential support during grid fluctuations. Existing literature has focused on isolated proton exchange membrane (PEM) electrolyzer models and, to some extent, grid-connected setups using electromagnetic transient (EMT) model. Phasor models are computationally efficient, ideal for large-scale power system studies, significantly reduce simulation times compared to EMT models. This paper proposes a comprehensive model of a grid-connected PEM hydrogen electrolyzer including the DC side electrochemical and electrical behavior of the electrolyzer and AC side phasor model and droop control of inverter simultaneously. Electrochemical dynamics of the DC side is modeled in detail including the operational constraints and DC link voltage control. An aggregated converter model consists of 220 droop-controlled modules each having 500 kVA rating is used for grid connection of the electrolyzer in Kundur's Two-Area Four-Machine Test System. This paper also studies the impact of grid-forming services and grid disturbances on the electrolyzer's physical features such as hydrogen stack voltage, temperature, and efficiency

articleTitle: Optimal Power Flow Incorporating RES in Microgrid Employing Hybrid Particle Swarm Optimization-Artificial Protozoa Optimizer
abstract: The electricity market's structure is experiencing significant changes due to the rise of renewable energy sources (RES). The unpredictable and irregular characteristics of RES presents a major obstacle to efficiently and affordably operating the grid. The mathematical model for optimizing power flow is highly complex, with both non-convex and nonlinear characteristics. Integrating RES into the grid for stability and reliability adds further complexity. This paper introduces a novel approach, combining Particle Swarm Optimization with Artificial Protozoa Optimization (HPS-APO), aimed at determining the most efficient schedule for a hybrid renewable energy system comprising windplants, solar plants and thermal generators. It accounts for the variability of solar power output and wind power output in grid operations, forecasting their output using probability density functions (pdfs) such as Lognormal distributions and Weibull distribution. Additionally, the costs associated with overestimation and underestimation in real-world scenarios are taken into consideration. Promising results are obtained while testing the proposed HPS-APO algorithm against alternative metaheuristic techniques on a modified IEEE-30 bus system. The proposed HPS-APO is tested on CEC 2022 benchmark functions and compared with the existing metaheuristic methods. The results show the efficacy and accuracy of the proposed HPS-APO algorithm.

articleTitle: Western Regional Experience of Renewable Energy Integration: First Time Energisation & Integration - Regulations & Compliances
abstract: Smooth integration of renewable energy (RE) resources to the grid and speeding up their integration while ensuring compliance with technical standards and other statutory and regulatory requirements is a vibrant area across the globe. First-Time Energisation and Integration (FTE&I) of RE generators along with their Associated Transmission System (ATS) has a significant operational impact on the electric grid. More so, the grid operators need to perform several compliance checks of various technical standards and regulatory norms for it. To ensure smooth and swift RE integration certain steps and procedures followed by the Western Regional Load Despatch Centre (WRLDC), Mumbai, are described in this paper. In addition, for attaining the ambitious renewable integration goals, the way ahead is described in brief.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Machine Learning Algorithms for Chhattisgarh State
abstract: The process of predicting future load patterns based on historical data and probabilities is commonly known as load forecasting. Different assessment can be used depending on the model and time scale such as short-term load forecasting (STLF), medium term load forecasting, long term load forecasting. This paper incorporates STLF approach to forecast the upcoming (i.e. next day) load demand values, specifically for Chhattisgarh State. STLF approach involves machine learning models like Regression Tree, Linear Regression, Kernel Approximation Regression, Ensembles of tree, SVM (Support vector machines) and ANN (Artificial neural network). The prediction process involves historical data along with its temperature and wind speed. Historical data (last 7 days of load values) along with current load demand and generation data of 25 Dec 2021 TO 31 Mar 2024 are collected from Chhattisgarh State Load Dispatch Centre, whereas temperature and wind speed data are collected from NASA Power prediction of worldwide energy resources. After prediction, the results are evaluated through statistical matrices i.e. MAPE, MAE, and overall performance of all models are compared.

articleTitle: A Novel Hybrid Algorithm for Charging Station Planning Problem
abstract: The ever-growing population of India, along with contemporaneous anticipation about exhaustion of fossil fuels and global warming, have rendered it necessary to create alternative modes of transportation. Electric vehicles (EV) are becoming increasingly popular in India. The establishment of charging facility is critical for widespread embrace of EV. Nevertheless, wrongful Electric Vehicle charging station (EVCS) planning compromises the electrical grid's reliability. The present investigation establishes and resolves the cs allocation issue for a distribution network (DN), as well as the precise position of distribution generators (DG). The geographical distribution of CS and DG is structured in single-objective paradigm including economic considerations and grid features such as voltage stability, dependability, and power loss in DN. The positioning challenge is handled employing an upgraded blended approach that combines Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Teaching Learning Based Optimization (TLBO) techniques, taking the most advantageous characteristics from both. The suggested approach has been evaluated on IEEE 33 bus network. The findings reveal that adequate design optimizations for DG size and position result in considerable reductions in power losses and improvements in voltage profile, as well as enhancement in total DN performance, hence mitigating the detrimental consequences of CS installation.
